tools.name: Claude in Chrome (Claude for Chrome)

variants.name: Claude in Chrome side panel (runs as a Cowork session on Max/Team, rolling out to Pro)
Browser tools for Claude Code (claude --chrome, VS Code extension)
variants.note: Exposed to Claude Code as the claude-in-chrome MCP server over a native messaging host and bridge.claudeusercontent.com; requires a claude.ai login (not API keys or third-party providers).

variants.name: Browser use from Cowork (Preferred browser: Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser)

summary: A Chrome (and Edge / Chromium) extension that lets Claude read, click, type and navigate in the user's own browser with the user's live login state, from the side panel, from Cowork, or as tools for Claude Code. Inference runs on the Anthropic API under the signed-in claude.ai account (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise); page content, screenshots and actions leave the browser to Anthropic, and side-panel sessions are saved to history and synced across devices. Modelling it as a personal autonomous agent is a stretch: it is a vendor extension that inherits the user's identity in every site it touches rather than an agent with its own runtime, and several pinned controls (sandboxing, EDR, transport) apply only at the browser boundary.

Anthropic's safeguards are model training, injection classifiers and action screening (reported attack success under 0.08% on internal testing), default-blocked site categories (adult, piracy; financial sites need explicit permission), prohibited actions (captcha solving, stock trading, facial images) and always-confirm actions (downloads, sensitive data entry, publishing, payments). Admin controls sit in the claude.ai console at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome: an org enable toggle (on by default on Team; off by default on Enterprise until 10 September 2026), site allowlists and blocklists that override user permissions, a per-role capability on Enterprise, and forceLoginOrgUUID as a Chrome enterprise policy. Users choose Manually approve, Automatically approve or Skip all approvals per task.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; extension 1.0.36+ for Claude Code; not through Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API with the claude.ai login; Claude Code sessions reach the extension through bridge.claudeusercontent.com, which must share the proxy egress used for claude.ai when IP allowlisting is on.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Page content, DOM and screenshots of the tabs Claude works in, console and network readers when used, and uploaded files (up to 10 MB) go to Anthropic; GIF recordings capture everything visible including logged-in account details.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Follows the account's plan policy (commercial: no training, 30-day retention); side-panel sessions are Cowork sessions saved to history.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: support.claude.com Claude in Chrome articles (get started, safety, permissions, admin controls) and code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome

riskNotes.note: Web content is the attack surface; ShadowPrompt (March 2026, fixed 1.0.41) let any site inject prompts through a trusted *.claude.ai subdomain, and Anthropic's own safety article calls the product "still risky". Allowlists and separate browser profiles are the practical containment.

Claude acts inside every session the user is logged into (Gmail, GitHub, Drive, banking if permitted) with no separate identity; ClaudeBleed (May 2026) showed another zero-permission extension could issue commands to it.
The extension requests 14 permissions including debugger, scripting and downloads; the native messaging host for Claude Code runs outside the corporate launcher.
"Skip all approvals" disables safety checks entirely; "Automatically approve" is the Cowork default. Publishing, sending messages and payments still require confirmation in the approving modes.
Screenshots and page text of authenticated apps leave the browser; Anthropic advises against use for financial, legal, medical or regulated data.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic-side injection classifiers, RL-trained refusals and automatic action screening; no admin-tunable detector

steps.title: Keep the approving modes on
body: Advise users to stay in Manually approve or Automatically approve; Skip all approvals turns off the safety checks that screen actions.

steps.title: Reduce exposure with allowlists and profiles
body: Start with a restrictive org allowlist and recommend a separate browser profile for sensitive accounts, per the safety guidance.

controls.mechanism: Org enable toggle "Enable for your team" at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome, per-role capability on Enterprise custom roles (separate from Cowork access), forceLoginOrgUUID deployable as a Chrome enterprise policy

steps.title: Decide who gets the extension
body: At Organization settings > Claude in Chrome set "Enable for your team" (Team default on; Enterprise default off until 10 September 2026) and grant the Claude in Chrome capability per custom role on Enterprise.

steps.title: Pin the extension to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID through Chrome enterprise policy so the extension can only be used with your Claude organisation.

controls.mechanism: Org allowlist / blocklist enforced regardless of user permission; built-in prohibited actions and always-confirm actions; in Claude Code, permission rules and PreToolUse hooks on the claude-in-chrome MCP tools

steps.title: Enforce site policy centrally
body: Add approved sites to the allowlist and forbidden sites to the blocklist under Organization settings > Claude in Chrome; the blocklist applies regardless of user settings and beyond the default blocked categories.

steps.title: Gate browser tools in Claude Code
body: Deny or ask on mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools in managed permissions, or block the server with deniedMcpServers so the install prompt never appears.

controls.mechanism: Extension to Anthropic over TLS; Claude Code to extension over a native messaging host plus a WebSocket bridge (bridge.claudeusercontent.com); extension-to-extension messaging was the ClaudeBleed weakness

steps.title: Route the bridge through the same egress
body: Send bridge.claudeusercontent.com through the same proxy egress as claude.ai and api.anthropic.com so IP allowlisting does not break it and traffic stays inspected.

controls.mechanism: Side-panel sessions are Cowork sessions saved to account history; per-site permission history in extension settings; no admin memory controls

steps.title: Review saved permissions
body: Users open Extension settings > Permissions to review approved sites and revoke access; session history follows Cowork retention.

controls.note: The agent acts inside the user's real browser profile and sessions by design; no isolated profile, container or VM is provided. Use a separate browser profile per the vendor's advice and Chrome enterprise policies for isolation.

controls.mechanism: Per-site permissions (Allow this action / Always allow actions on this site), org allowlist and blocklist, default-blocked categories, financial sites require explicit permission, Claude Code plan-mode read-only tool split

steps.title: Scope by site
body: Configure the org allowlist so Claude can only browse approved sites; users then grant per-site actions and can revoke them in Extension settings.

controls.note: Claude uses the user's existing logins in every site; there is no separate agent identity or on-behalf-of exchange. Prohibited actions (sensitive data entry, downloads need approval) are the only mitigation.
The extension holds the claude.ai session; site credentials are the browser's. Nothing to vault; keep sensitive accounts in a separate profile.

controls.mechanism: Built-in blocked site categories, prohibited actions and always-confirm actions; Anthropic safety classifiers; no admin-editable policy beyond site lists

steps.title: Layer the org blocklist over the defaults
body: The blocklist adds to Claude's default blocked categories; use it for regulated systems the safety guidance says not to automate.

controls.mechanism: In Claude Code the extension is the reserved claude-in-chrome MCP server governed by managed MCP allow/deny lists; the extension itself comes from the Chrome Web Store

steps.title: Allow or block the server organisation-wide
body: List claude-in-chrome in deniedMcpServers to block it (Claude Code then never prompts to install the extension), or in allowedMcpServers to permit it.

controls.mechanism: Manually approve (plan shown before acting), Automatically approve (pauses on flagged risks), always-confirm actions; Claude Code prompts "Claude in Chrome wants to" per site

steps.title: Set the approval mode
body: Choose Manually approve to review a plan naming the sites before any action; Automatically approve still requires approval for publishing, messaging, payments, downloads and sensitive data entry.

controls.mechanism: Usage draws from the account's plan limits and organisation usage limits; scheduled shortcuts run recurring tasks; no per-task action budget

steps.title: Bound spend at the organisation
body: Set organisation, group and user usage limits under Organization settings > Usage; the consumption guide notes Claude in Chrome does not yet honour model and effort restrictions.

controls.mechanism: Side-panel sessions are Cowork sessions (transcripts retrievable through the Compliance API on Enterprise); per-site permission history; Claude Code tool events via OpenTelemetry

steps.title: Retrieve session transcripts
body: Enterprise organisations pull Cowork local and remote session transcripts, including side-panel sessions, through the Compliance API session endpoints.

controls.note: Browser actions themselves are visible only as tool calls in the transcript; there is no separate action log for the extension.

controls.mechanism: Org toggle off, role capability removal, Chrome enterprise policy (extension blocklist / force-uninstall), user revocation of site permissions

steps.title: Turn it off for the organisation
body: Disable "Enable for your team" at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome or remove the capability from roles; pair with Chrome enterprise extension policy to uninstall.

controls.mechanism: Chrome enterprise extension inventory and policy; tenant-restriction header blocks personal claude.ai accounts

steps.title: Inventory and pin the extension
body: Use Chrome enterprise policy to list installed extensions and inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the proxy so the extension cannot be used with a personal account.

controls.mechanism: Browser and endpoint sensors; the native messaging host is started by the browser, outside Claude Code's corporate launcher
controls.note: The corporate-launcher page states the Chrome native-messaging host is not covered by processWrapper; EDR must watch it directly.

steps.title: Cover the native messaging host
body: Monitor com.anthropic.claude_code_browser_extension host registrations and the process it starts with endpoint tooling.

controls.note: No baseline or drift detection is offered; the classifier screens individual actions only.

controls.mechanism: Always-confirm on sensitive data entry and downloads; org blocklist for data-bearing sites; Read deny rules govern uploads from Claude Code

steps.title: Block uploads of protected files from Claude Code
body: Permission rules that deny Read on a file also block uploading it through the extension; uploads are capped at 10 MB.

controls.note: There is no registry of which users have the extension beyond Chrome enterprise inventory; scheduled shortcuts are per user.

controls.mechanism: Org allowlist restricts browsing destinations; bridge.claudeusercontent.com and api.anthropic.com are the only vendor endpoints

steps.title: Use the allowlist as the egress policy
body: Approve only the sites Claude may open; Claude in Manually approve mode uses only the sites listed in its plan.

controls.note: Not applicable: no model artifacts run locally.

ClaudeBleed — zero-permission Chrome extensions could issue commands to Claude in Chrome; partial fix in 1.0.70 bypassed

tools.name: Claude Code

variants.name: Claude Code CLI
Claude Code for VS Code
Claude Code for JetBrains IDEs
variants.note: The plugin runs a local, unauthenticated-transport (ws://) MCP server bound to loopback; the docs warn that acceptEdits mode can write IDE config files the IDE auto-executes.

variants.name: Claude Code Desktop (Code tab in Claude Desktop, local / SSH / WSL sessions)
variants.note: Local sessions read the device's managed settings; cloud sessions started from the Code tab are toolClaudeCodeWeb. Desktop-only keys: disableDesktopLocalSessions, sshHostAllowlist, disableBrowserExternalNavigation, disableMobileSimulatorTools.

variants.name: Remote Control (claude.ai/code or the mobile app driving a local session)
variants.note: Execution stays on the developer's machine; the transcript is stored on Anthropic servers while connected. Off by default on Team/Enterprise until an Owner enables it; managed disableRemoteControl turns it off per device; unavailable under ZDR.

variants.name: Claude Code GitHub Actions (anthropics/claude-code-action)
variants.note: Runs the Agent SDK on GitHub-hosted runners. Auth by ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret, or keyless via workload identity federation (anthropic_federation_rule_id); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry via OIDC. Tools are opt-in with --allowedTools in claude_args; triggering actor must have write access and be human.

summary: Anthropic's agentic coding tool, run by a present developer as a CLI, an IDE extension (VS Code, JetBrains), the Code tab of Claude Desktop, or unattended as a GitHub Action. Inference runs on the Anthropic API by default; organisations can route it to Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (Vertex), Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, a self-hosted Claude apps gateway, or any LLM gateway via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. All prompts, tool results and file contents Claude reads leave the device to the configured provider over TLS; operational telemetry and error reports to Anthropic are on by default on the Anthropic API and off on third-party providers.

Two admin channels share one top-precedence managed tier: endpoint-managed settings delivered as files or OS policies via MDM/GPO (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode, managed-settings.json plus managed-settings.d/), and server-managed settings configured by Owners at claude.ai Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (Team/Enterprise) and fetched at startup with hourly polling. Managed settings outrank command-line flags and all user and project files. The docs state server-managed settings are a client-side control, not a security boundary, and that they are skipped when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY or a non-default ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set; endpoint policy or a Claude apps gateway is the enforcement channel there.

The enforcement points that matter are permissions.deny (evaluated before everything, cannot be overridden by any mode or the auto-mode classifier), PreToolUse hooks (fire in every permission mode including bypassPermissions), the OS-enforced Bash sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap with a domain-allowlisting proxy and credential masking), managed MCP allow/deny lists, plugin marketplace allowlists, and OpenTelemetry export of every tool decision to the organisation's collector.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise (claude.ai login), Claude Console API keys or keyless Console sign-in, and Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / Claude Platform on AWS credentials. Server-managed settings, analytics dashboard and SSO need Team/Enterprise; SCIM, Compliance API and ZDR need Enterprise.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API by default. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS select a cloud provider; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN route through an LLM gateway; forceLoginMethod "gateway" plus forceLoginGatewayUrl pin sessions to a self-hosted Claude apps gateway that holds the upstream credential, maps IdP groups to models and managed settings, and relays OTLP telemetry. Third-party routing disables server-managed settings, Remote Control, cloud sessions and the Chrome integration.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, model outputs and everything a tool returns go to the model provider over TLS 1.2+. Metrics (no code or prompts) and redacted error reports go to Anthropic and a third-party logging service by default on the Anthropic API; DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC turn them off. WebFetch sends each hostname to api.anthropic.com for a safety-blocklist check (skipWebFetchPreflight disables). /feedback uploads the transcript.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): no training; 30-day retention; ZDR available to qualified Enterprise accounts (disables cloud sessions, Remote Control, Claude Tag, artifacts and feedback). Consumer plans follow the user's training preference (5-year or 30-day retention). Local transcripts sit in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com (claude.ai connectors), downloads.claude.ai, registry.npmjs.org, bridge.claudeusercontent.com (Chrome), plus optional Datadog intake hosts for telemetry. HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT/KEY mTLS are supported; SOCKS is not.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: code.claude.com/docs (machine-readable map at claude_code_docs_map.md)

items.title: Managed settings via MDM, GPO or the admin console
body: Endpoint paths: macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json (plus a managed-settings.d/ drop-in directory), Linux and WSL /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json — the legacy ProgramData path is no longer read as of v2.1.75 (CVE-2026-35603). OS-policy channels: the macOS managed-preference domain com.anthropic.claudecode and the Windows registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode (HKCU is a user-writable fallback, not an enforcement channel).

Server-managed settings cover the same keys from Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (Owner role), with a caveat the docs state plainly: it is a client-side control, not a security boundary, and it is skipped when routing through Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a custom base URL. Endpoint management via MDM is the stronger channel; forceRemoteSettingsRefresh makes the server channel fail closed at startup. Cloud sessions read only server-managed settings; Cowork sessions never fetch them.

links.title: Claude Code settings reference (precedence, paths, keys)
Deploy managed settings (delivery mechanisms, precedence within the managed tier)

items.title: Permission, MCP and hook lockdown
body: Pin permission rules with permissions.allow / deny / ask, and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly to block user- and project-level rules (and --allowedTools) entirely. permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode and permissions.disableAutoMode remove the bypass and auto modes; autoMode.environment / hard_deny / soft_deny tune the auto-mode classifier, which the docs describe as a second gate after permissions.deny.

MCP admission: allowedMcpServers is the allowlist — undefined means unrestricted and an empty array is a full lockdown — with deniedMcpServers winning on conflict, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, managedMcpServers to push remote servers, and a managed-mcp.json file for exclusive control of MCP configuration. Hooks and sideloading close the remaining gaps: allowManagedHooksOnly, disableAllHooks, allowedHttpHookUrls, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces, disableCommandPluginSources, and disableSideloadFlags to reject --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at the command line.

links.title: Control MCP server access for your organization

items.title: Forced login, credentials and audit telemetry
body: forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID pin sessions to the organisation; forceLoginOrgUUID also blocks startup on ambient API-key credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, apiKeyHelper). apiKeyHelper substitutes a managed credential script for stored keys; credentials otherwise live in the macOS Keychain or a 0600 ~/.claude/.credentials.json.

Fleet-wide audit: set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and the OTEL_* exporter variables in the managed env block; when the exporter endpoint comes from managed settings, conflicting developer-set OTel variables are removed at startup. Sessions then emit per-tool decision events, prompt and API events (text redacted by default) and usage metrics to the organisation's collector. Enterprise organisations can also pull local Claude Code session transcripts through the Compliance API.

riskNotes.note: Every file, web page, MCP result and IDE selection Claude reads is untrusted input. Anthropic's own mitigations are the permission prompts, an auto-mode classifier, an isolated context window for WebFetch and command-injection detection; the docs are explicit that no system is immune and recommend VMs for untrusted content. The hard controls are permissions.deny, PreToolUse hooks and the sandbox network allowlist.

Project files (.mcp.json, .claude/settings.json hooks, CLAUDE.md) are configuration the repository author controls. CVE-2025-59536 and CVE-2026-21852 showed they could execute code or redirect ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL before the trust prompt. allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedHooksOnly, strictPluginOnlyCustomization and allowManagedMcpServersOnly move those decisions to the managed tier.

Read-only Bash commands can read the whole machine by default, including ~/.aws and ~/.ssh; sandbox.credentials deny/mask entries, sandbox.filesystem.denyRead and Read() deny rules are how an organisation fences secrets. Session transcripts are stored in plaintext locally and, with Remote Control, on Anthropic servers.

Auto mode is the built-in starting mode on Pro, Max and Team. There is no managed per-session token or turn budget in the CLI; spend is bounded at the organisation level (admin spend limits, Console workspace limits, or gateway per-user limits) and per run only through --max-turns in headless and GitHub Actions use.

Background agents (claude agents, --bg), agent teams, cross-session messaging and Remote Control all start Claude Code processes outside the developer's terminal; disableAgentView, processWrapper (corporate launcher), crossSessionInbound and disableRemoteControl are the switches.

controls.mechanism: claude.ai login pinned to the organisation (forceLoginMethod, forceLoginOrgUUID) with SSO/SCIM at the org level; Claude apps gateway for IdP sign-in on third-party providers

steps.title: Pin logins to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginMethod ("claudeai" or "console") and forceLoginOrgUUID (your org UUID from claude.ai/admin-settings/organization) through MDM or managed-settings.json; sessions on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper are then blocked at startup.

steps.title: Enforce SSO and SCIM at the organisation
body: Turn on "Require SSO for Claude" at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization after domain verification; Enterprise adds SCIM group-to-role mapping and automatic deprovisioning.

steps.title: On Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry use the Claude apps gateway
body: Run claude gateway with an OIDC IdP; developers sign in with corporate SSO, receive short-lived bearer tokens, and lose access when deprovisioned in the IdP.

controls.mechanism: permissions.deny / ask / allow rules in managed settings plus PreToolUse hooks (command, http, mcp_tool); deny rules and hooks run before every permission mode, including bypassPermissions and the auto-mode classifier

steps.title: Author deny rules that no mode can override
body: Put permissions.deny entries such as Bash(curl *), Read(./.env), Read(./secrets/**) and mcp__* patterns in managed settings and set allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly so user, project and --allowedTools rules are ignored.

steps.title: Add a PreToolUse policy hook
body: Deploy a managed hooks.PreToolUse entry whose command or HTTP endpoint returns permissionDecision "deny" or "ask"; hooks fire in every permission mode and a hook deny applies even with --dangerously-skip-permissions.

steps.title: Constrain the auto-mode classifier
body: Deliver an autoMode block (environment, hard_deny, soft_deny, allow, classifyAllShell) through managed settings; note the docs call the classifier a second gate that permissions.deny always precedes.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 artifacts) feeds the buyer's TPRM platform
controls.note: Vendor assurance artifacts are published at trust.anthropic.com and linked from the security page; the reassessment cadence and evidence expiry live in the organisation's own TPRM tooling, not in Claude Code.

steps.title: Collect vendor evidence from the Trust Center
body: Download the SOC 2 Type 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate referenced on the Claude Code security page and attach them to the vendor record.

controls.mechanism: Read() / Edit() deny rules, sandbox.credentials masking and sandbox.filesystem.denyRead keep named secrets out of the context; Enterprise Inference hooks send each governed prompt to the organisation's AI security server for an allow/deny verdict

steps.title: Exclude sensitive files from the context
body: Add permissions.deny rules such as Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*) and Read(//**/.pem) in managed settings; the JetBrains and VS Code extensions honour Read deny rules for selection sharing too.

steps.title: Mask credentials inside the sandbox
body: Set sandbox.credentials.files and sandbox.credentials.envVars with mode deny or mask so sandboxed commands see placeholders and the proxy re-injects the real value only for allowed hosts.

steps.title: Inspect prompts inline with Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta)
body: Configure an AI security server endpoint; Anthropic POSTs each governed Claude Code prompt transcript for an allow/deny verdict before inference, with shadow mode and rollout percentages.

controls.mechanism: permissions.allow/ask/deny with tool specifiers, bare-name deny rules that remove a tool from Claude's context, permissions.defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode, disableAutoMode, additionalDirectories and blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories

steps.title: Fix the starting permission mode and remove escape hatches
body: In managed settings set permissions.defaultMode, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable" and permissions.disableAutoMode "disable" (auto mode can also be turned off for the organisation on Team and Enterprise).

steps.title: Remove tools or scope them
body: A bare deny such as "WebFetch" or "mcp__*" removes the tool from context; scoped rules like Bash(git push *) in permissions.ask force a prompt even in auto mode.

steps.title: Fence file access
body: Set permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories true and control permissions.additionalDirectories so reads and edits stay inside approved roots in every mode.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.* block (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap plus socat on Linux/WSL2; not native Windows) with filesystem allow/deny paths, a hostname-allowlisting network proxy, failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands false

steps.title: Require the sandbox fleet-wide
body: Set sandbox.enabled true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable true and sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands false in managed settings so commands cannot fall back to running unsandboxed.

steps.title: Lock the filesystem and network lists to managed settings
body: Use sandbox.filesystem.denyRead / allowWrite with sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly, and sandbox.network.allowedDomains with sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly; these lock keys are honoured from any admin-controlled source.

steps.title: Know the limits
body: The proxy allowlists by client-supplied hostname and does not terminate TLS unless sandbox.network.tlsTerminate is set; the sandbox shares the host kernel. Use dev containers or VMs for untrusted content.

controls.mechanism: apiKeyHelper rotating credentials, Claude apps gateway holding the upstream key, sandbox credential masking with per-host re-injection, and per-purpose short-lived Remote Control credentials; the agent otherwise acts with the developer's own identity

steps.title: Keep the model credential out of the developer's hands
body: Route through a Claude apps gateway (developers hold only short-lived gateway tokens) or set apiKeyHelper to a vault-backed script with CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS.

steps.title: Inject tool credentials at the proxy, not in the shell
body: Use sandbox.credentials.envVars mask entries with sandbox.network.tlsTerminate so the sandbox holds placeholders and the proxy substitutes the secret only for allowed hosts; AWS SigV4 re-signing is supported via credentials.awsPairs.

controls.note: Git, cloud CLI and MCP tools still run as the developer; there is no on-behalf-of exchange or delegation-chain tracking in the local product.

controls.mechanism: autoMemoryEnabled, autoMemoryDirectory, claudeMd (managed org-wide CLAUDE.md), claudeMdExcludes, cleanupPeriodDays and fileCheckpointingEnabled in settings

steps.title: Decide whether auto memory runs
body: Set autoMemoryEnabled false (or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 in env) to stop Claude writing persistent memories under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, or point autoMemoryDirectory at a governed location.

steps.title: Bound transcript retention on the device
body: Set cleanupPeriodDays (default 30) and desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays so plaintext session transcripts are pruned.

controls.note: Memory files are plain Markdown the agent edits with ordinary Write/Edit tools; there is no validation, quarantine or rollback of memory contents beyond file checkpoints.

controls.mechanism: Built-in context-aware analysis, command-injection detection, fail-closed command matching, an isolated context window for WebFetch, the auto-mode classifier's exfiltration rules, and the WebFetch hostname safety check

steps.title: Keep the built-in safeguards on
body: Do not set skipWebFetchPreflight; keep permissions.deny for curl/wget and rely on the auto-mode classifier's built-in hard_deny data-exfiltration rule by including "$defaults" in any autoMode override.

steps.title: Treat repositories and MCP servers as untrusted
body: Trust verification runs for new folders and MCP servers in interactive mode only (not with -p); use managed MCP allowlists and strictPluginOnlyCustomization so a checked-in file cannot add tools or hooks.

controls.note: These are model- and heuristic-based; Anthropic states no system is immune. There is no admin-configurable classifier or third-party detector hook in the local product beyond PreToolUse hooks and Enterprise Inference hooks.

controls.mechanism: apiKeyHelper / otelHeadersHelper / awsCredentialExport / gcpAuthRefresh scripts for rotating credentials; macOS Keychain or 0600 credentials file; CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and GitHub Actions secrets or workload identity federation for CI

steps.title: Use helper scripts instead of static keys
body: Set apiKeyHelper (re-run every five minutes by default) to fetch a short-lived token from your vault; forceLoginOrgUUID blocks ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY use.

steps.title: Go keyless in CI
body: In GitHub Actions pass anthropic_federation_rule_id and anthropic_organization_id with id-token write so the workflow exchanges its OIDC token for Claude API access through a Console service account; on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry use OIDC as well.

controls.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers / allowManagedMcpServersOnly / managedMcpServers, exclusive managed-mcp.json, disableClaudeAiConnectors, org connector tool controls (ask / blocked), strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces for plugins

steps.title: Deploy a fixed server set or an allowlist
body: Place managed-mcp.json in the system directory for exclusive control (an empty mcpServers object disables MCP entirely), or deliver allowedMcpServers plus allowManagedMcpServersOnly through server-managed settings.

steps.title: Restrict plugin and marketplace sources
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces to an allowlist (an empty array blocks every marketplace), blockedMarketplaces, disableCommandPluginSources true and disableSideloadFlags true.

steps.title: Mark sensitive MCP tools as always-ask
body: Servers can set _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction so a tool always prompts; claude.ai connector tools an Owner sets to ask or blocked are enforced in every mode.

controls.note: Anthropic reviews Directory connectors against listing criteria but does not security-audit MCP servers; there is no content-hash pinning of tool definitions.

controls.mechanism: Manual permission mode, permissions.ask rules (honoured even in auto mode), plan mode, PreToolUse hooks returning "ask", and GitHub Actions gating by write access and human actor

steps.title: Force a human checkpoint on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask entries such as Bash(git push *) and Bash(gh pr create *); an explicit ask rule prompts even when auto mode or an allow rule would otherwise approve.

steps.title: Keep the mode set that asks
body: Set permissions.defaultMode "default" and disable auto and bypass modes so edits and non-read-only commands prompt; Accept Edits still asks outside the working directory and for critical paths.

controls.mechanism: Seat assignment and per-role Claude Code capability in the claude.ai admin console; disableAgentView, agent teams and cross-session messaging flags; the analytics dashboard lists active users and sessions

steps.title: Gate who may run Claude Code
body: Assign Claude Code access by seat (Organization settings > Organization) and, on Enterprise, by custom role and group under Organization settings > Roles.

steps.title: Control background and peer agents
body: Set disableAgentView true to turn off claude agents, --bg and the supervisor; crossSessionInbound and isolatePeerMachines govern cross-session messaging.

controls.note: There is no registry of agents or tool servers with owners and approval state; the analytics dashboard and OpenTelemetry attributes (organization.id, user.account_uuid, session.id) are the inventory.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry events (claude_code.tool_decision, tool_result, user_prompt, api_request) with user.account_uuid and organization.id; Compliance API local-session transcripts (Enterprise); ConfigChange hooks; server-managed settings change audit

steps.title: Export tool decisions fleet-wide
body: In the managed env block set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; developer overrides of the exporter are removed at startup. Add OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 only if the collector may hold commands.

steps.title: Pull transcripts after the fact
body: Enterprise organisations retrieve Claude Code local-session transcripts (prompts, tool calls, results; 6-year retention by default) with a Compliance Access Key and the read:compliance_user_data scope.

steps.title: Audit settings edits
body: Add a ConfigChange hook to log or block user_settings / project_settings changes; policy_settings changes cannot be blocked and server-managed changes are audited through the Compliance API.

controls.mechanism: Tenant restrictions header (anthropic-allowed-org-ids) injected by the corporate proxy; the analytics dashboard shows who is active; endpoint tooling finds unmanaged installs
controls.note: Claude Code does not discover unsanctioned installs; the vendor lever is the proxy-injected tenant-restrictions header that blocks personal-account use, plus IP allowlisting. Pair with EDR/SSE inventory of the claude binary and ~/.claude directories.

steps.title: Block personal accounts on the corporate network
body: Configure the TLS-inspecting proxy to inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your org UUIDs for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com.

controls.mechanism: Seat removal / SCIM deprovisioning, /logout revocation, requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh fail-closed startup, and disableRemoteControl / disableAgentView

steps.title: Cut access at the identity layer
body: Remove the seat or SCIM group; Console API keys are deleted in the Console; a gateway sign-in expires within the session lifetime (one hour by default).

steps.title: Refuse to start outside policy
body: Deliver requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion, and set forceRemoteSettingsRefresh true so clients exit when the server policy cannot be fetched.

controls.note: Running sessions keep working until credentials expire; there is no server-side "stop all sessions" for local clients. Local transcripts must be deleted on the device.

controls.mechanism: processWrapper / CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER corporate launcher for every self-spawned process; OTel tool events feed the SIEM; WSL sessions need an in-distro Linux sensor

steps.title: Route every Claude Code process through the corporate launcher
body: Set processWrapper (or env CLAUDE_CODE_PROCESS_WRAPPER) in managed settings to your launcher's absolute path; it wraps the background service, agent-view sessions and Remote Control processes (not Windows).

steps.title: Cover WSL sessions
body: Windows-side sensors do not see WSL 2 processes; run your EDR vendor's Linux sensor inside the distribution or rely on the identical OTel tool-execution telemetry.

controls.mechanism: Managed policy CLAUDE.md (claudeMd key or file at the managed policy path), claudeMdExcludes, strictPluginOnlyCustomization for agents/hooks/skills, includeGitInstructions

steps.title: Deploy organisation-wide instructions
body: Put org instructions in the managed claudeMd key or the managed policy CLAUDE.md path; they load in every session and cannot be excluded by users.

steps.title: Lock custom agents, skills and hooks to managed or plugin sources
body: Set strictPluginOnlyCustomization true (or its agents / hooks / mcp sub-keys) so user and project sources cannot add instructions that run with tool access.

controls.note: Project and user CLAUDE.md files remain untrusted instruction sources loaded into the same context; there is no structural hierarchy separating them from managed instructions.

The vendor ships pinned versions (requiredMinimumVersion, SDK-bundled binary, plugin archive SHA-256 digests) but no signed manifest of the models, plugins and MCP servers a session composes; the March 2026 npm source-map exposure showed release packaging is not attested. Generate an AI-BOM from managed settings, managed-mcp.json and the plugin marketplace lockfile yourself.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.network.allowedDomains / deniedDomains / strictAllowlist / allowManagedDomainsOnly, WebFetch(domain:) rules, permissions.deny for curl/wget, HTTPS_PROXY / NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, and the documented outbound host list

steps.title: Allowlist sandbox egress from managed settings
body: Set sandbox.network.allowedDomains, sandbox.network.strictAllowlist true and sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly true; non-allowed hosts are then blocked instead of prompting, for Bash and its child processes.

steps.title: Restrict the fetch tool and network commands
body: Deny WebFetch or allow only WebFetch(domain:host) entries, and deny Bash(curl *) and Bash(wget *); the docs note deny rules match the command as written, so pair them with the sandbox allowlist.

steps.title: Pin the proxy and firewall allowlist
body: Deliver HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS in the managed env block and allow only the documented hosts (api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, platform.claude.com, downloads.claude.ai, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com and so on) at the firewall.

controls.note: Not applicable to the product: Claude Code loads no model artifacts locally; inference is remote on the configured provider. Nothing to scan on the endpoint.

variants.name: claude.ai/code and the Claude mobile app

Routines (scheduled cloud sessions), Code Review and Ultrareview
variants.note: Features of the same cloud runtime; Code Review is Team/Enterprise only.

variants.name: Self-hosted environments (runners on your infrastructure, public beta)
variants.note: Execution moves to your network; orchestration, queueing, the transcript and inference stay with Anthropic. Not routable through Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or an LLM gateway.

summary: Claude Code sessions that run on Anthropic-managed VMs (research preview for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise premium / Chat + Claude Code seats) rather than on the developer's machine. The VM clones the GitHub repository, works on a branch, and can open pull requests; a security proxy carries git and MCP traffic with scoped credentials so the user's GitHub token never enters the sandbox. Sessions persist after the browser closes, can be driven from the mobile app, Slack (Claude Tag) or the CLI, and are reclaimed after inactivity. Organisations that need execution on their own network run self-hosted environments; inference still goes to api.anthropic.com with a session-scoped OAuth token.

Admin control is server-side only: device managed-settings files and MDM policies do not reach cloud sessions, so policy comes from server-managed settings (claude.ai Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings), organisation-shared cloud environments (network access level, environment variables, setup script) and the Claude Code admin toggles (Code in the web, allow_remote_sessions, Quick web setup, Remote Control, Routines). Prompts, code and outputs follow the account's retention policy; ZDR organisations cannot use cloud sessions at all, and the Compliance API does not return Claude Code web transcripts.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Research preview on Pro, Max and Team; Enterprise with premium or Chat + Claude Code seats. Not available through Console API keys, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or ZDR organisations. Repositories must be on GitHub (GHES supported on Team/Enterprise); non-GitHub repos can be sent as a bundle but cannot push back.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API from Anthropic-managed infrastructure (so organisation IP allowlists block it unless Anthropic-hosted services are exempted); self-hosted environments call the API from your network with a session-scoped OAuth token and cannot route through a cloud provider or gateway.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: The repository is cloned into an isolated VM; all outbound traffic passes a security proxy for audit logging; GitHub credentials stay outside the sandbox; with network access "No access" the VM can still reach the Anthropic API, which the docs note may allow data to exit.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Same commercial policy as local Claude Code (no training on Team/Enterprise/API, 30-day retention); session event data is deleted when a user deletes the session; ZDR organisations have cloud sessions disabled at the backend.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: code.claude.com/docs (Claude Code on the web, Cloud environments, Self-hosted environments)

riskNotes.note: A cloud session can reach any repository the connecting GitHub account can see, not just repositories the Claude GitHub App is installed on; restrict at GitHub. Shared environments' variables are readable by every member's sessions, so secrets must not go there (API credentials that stay outside the sandbox exist only on Pro/Max today).
Auto-fix replies to PR comments and pushes fixes under the user's GitHub account and can trigger comment-driven automation such as Atlantis; git push is restricted to the working branch.

Sessions started from Slack read the whole thread as context; the earlier Claude Code in Slack docs warn Claude may follow directions from other messages. Network egress in Anthropic-hosted environments defaults to Trusted (package registries and GitHub), which bounds exfiltration.
Any member with a seat can start cloud sessions once "Code in the web" is on; Routines run unattended on a schedule. Admin toggles and organisation-default environments are the inventory levers.

controls.mechanism: claude.ai organisation login with SSO/SCIM; per-role Claude Code capability on Enterprise; Owner-only admin toggles at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by seat and role
body: Assign Claude Code seats and, on Enterprise, grant the Claude Code capability to custom roles under Organization settings > Roles; sessions always use the subscription login (API keys cannot start them).

steps.title: Decide whether the web surface exists
body: Owners turn "Code in the web", the allow_remote_sessions policy, Remote Control and Quick web setup on or off at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code.

controls.mechanism: Sessions run under the user's account with proxy-issued scoped git credentials; self-hosted runners register with an environment key and receive runner tokens; Claude Tag channel sessions run under an agent identity

steps.title: Treat the environment key as a workload credential
body: The environment secret shown once at creation authenticates every runner; store it in a secrets manager and rotate it from the Cloud environments admin page.

controls.note: Anthropic-hosted sessions have no distinct agent identity: GitHub actions appear as the user (or the Claude GitHub App). Session identity can be verified by your own services in self-hosted environments.

controls.mechanism: GitHub proxy keeps git credentials and signing keys outside the sandbox; API credentials attached by the agent proxy per host (Pro/Max only); environment variables are readable by the session

steps.title: Never put secrets in environment variables
body: Every session in a shared environment can read its variables and setup script; on Pro/Max store keys as API credentials with allowed hosts instead. Team and Enterprise do not have API credentials yet.

steps.title: Supply git credentials from your own store in self-hosted environments
body: Configure per-session minted credentials or the Anthropic git proxy in the runner deployment rather than baking tokens into the runner image.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic infrastructure-level AES-256 disk encryption and TLS in transit; no CMEK for cloud sessions
controls.note: The data-usage page documents infrastructure encryption at rest for the Anthropic API; customer-managed keys are an Enterprise chat feature and are not offered for cloud session storage.

steps.title: Confirm the encryption posture
body: Review the encryption-at-rest table (Anthropic API: AES-256 infrastructure encryption; ZDR removes server-side persistence but disables cloud sessions).

controls.mechanism: Session list at claude.ai/code with Team visibility on Team/Enterprise; organisation-shared and self-hosted environments managed by Owners on the Cloud environments admin page; Routines listed per user

steps.title: Centralise environments
body: Owners create organisation-shared environments and set the organisation default on the Cloud environments page; Admins cannot open it. Members' own environments are personal to their account.

controls.note: There is no approval workflow or owner record for sessions or routines beyond the user who created them.
Cloud environments are not versioned and sessions pick up the current settings; the docs advise keeping your own change record. No canary or rollback of environment or policy changes is offered.

controls.mechanism: Server-managed settings (permissions.allow/ask/deny, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, disableAutoMode) apply to cloud sessions; permission mode is chosen per session from the web UI; connectors filtered by allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers

steps.title: Deliver the same permission policy as the desktop fleet
body: Configure permissions.deny, disableBypassPermissionsMode and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly under Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings; endpoint-managed files do not reach Anthropic-hosted sessions.

steps.title: Filter connectors in cloud sessions
body: Connectors are passed to the cloud VM and filtered by the organisation's allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers patterns; disableSideloadFlags drops servers the server delivered through --mcp-config.

controls.mechanism: Per-session permission mode picker (Accept edits, Plan, Auto; Bypass unavailable in cloud sessions), permissions.ask rules from server-managed settings, MCP connector tool approvals that pause the session

steps.title: Force prompts on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask rules such as Bash(git push *) in server-managed settings; the session waits for the user (and expires if it waits too long) rather than auto-approving.

steps.title: Review before merge
body: Sessions produce a diff and a PR rather than merging; auto-fix acts only on PRs where the toggle is on, and the docs recommend disabling it where a PR comment can deploy infrastructure.

controls.mechanism: Same built-in safeguards as local Claude Code plus the auto-mode classifier and a default-limited network egress; Enterprise Inference hooks apply to Claude Code sessions

steps.title: Keep egress at Trusted or Custom
body: Set the environment's network access level to Trusted (default) or a Custom allowlist so an injected instruction cannot reach arbitrary hosts.

steps.title: Add inline prompt inspection (Enterprise, beta)
body: Configure Inference hooks so every governed Claude Code prompt is sent to your AI security server for an allow/deny verdict before inference.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center artifacts (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001) into the buyer's TPRM platform
controls.note: Vendor evidence is published; cadence and reassessment are the organisation's own TPRM process.

steps.title: Attach vendor evidence
body: Pull the Trust Center reports linked from the Claude Code security page into the vendor record; the cloud execution section documents the isolation claims to assess.

controls.mechanism: Session transcript and diff view at claude.ai/code; all outbound traffic through the security proxy is logged for audit; self-hosted runners expose metrics and a health endpoint and forward OTel from sessions

steps.title: Read the session record
body: Each session keeps the full conversation, tool activity and per-file diffs, visible to the user and (with Team visibility) the organisation.

steps.title: Export runner and session telemetry when self-hosting
body: The runner honours the OpenTelemetry variables from network-config and sessions inherit them; the reference lists runner metrics and the health endpoint.

controls.note: Anthropic-hosted sessions do not expose an OTLP export to the organisation's collector and the Compliance API does not return Claude Code web transcripts.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic logs all cloud-session operations and proxy traffic for compliance; admin console changes appear in the Enterprise audit log / Compliance API Activity Feed; session transcripts are not exported

steps.title: Export admin and settings events
body: Enterprise Owners export audit logs (180 days) from Organization settings > Data and privacy or query the Compliance API Activity Feed; server-managed settings changes are audited there.

controls.note: The Compliance API session endpoints explicitly exclude Claude Code on the web; the vendor's own operation logs are not customer-accessible.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's model-side safety systems, the auto-mode classifier, and organisation model restrictions / effort caps enforced server-side for claude.ai members

steps.title: Restrict models and effort for the organisation
body: On Enterprise, disable individual models and cap effort per role from the organisation admin settings; these are enforced server-side for claude.ai sign-ins.

controls.note: No admin-configurable topic or content filter exists for cloud sessions.

controls.mechanism: Session VMs are reclaimed after inactivity and conversation history is restored on reopen; users can delete sessions permanently; auto memory follows the repository's settings

steps.title: Delete sessions and bound the VM lifetime
body: Users delete sessions (event data removed permanently) from the sidebar; VMs are automatically reclaimed after inactivity and background work is not restored.

controls.note: No evaluation harness or release gate is exposed for cloud sessions; the vendor's own model evaluations are published in system cards, not as a customer control.

controls.mechanism: Claude Code analytics dashboard and Enterprise Analytics API feed the organisation's governance system of record

steps.title: Pull adoption data into your governance platform
body: Use the analytics dashboard at claude.ai/analytics/claude-code or the Enterprise Analytics API (read:analytics key) for per-user engagement and cost reports.

controls.mechanism: Cloud sessions share the account's rate limits; organisation and per-user spend limits in the admin console; no per-session budget or time cap

steps.title: Set organisation, group and user spend limits
body: Configure limits under Organization settings > Usage (org default, by group, per user); Claude Code, Cowork and chat draw from the same consumption pool.

controls.note: Sessions stop only when the account's limits are exhausted; there is no turn or wall-clock cap for a cloud session.

controls.mechanism: Owner toggles (Code in the web, allow_remote_sessions, Remote Control, Allow self-hosted environments), seat removal, session archive/delete, runner --retire-at and SIGTERM drain

steps.title: Turn the surface off
body: Owners disable "Code in the web" and allow_remote_sessions at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code; new cloud sessions then fail with a policy error.

steps.title: Stop runners cleanly
body: Self-hosted runners drain on SIGTERM or at --retire-at, releasing sessions so they resume elsewhere; revoking the environment key stops new claims.

controls.note: Running Anthropic-hosted sessions are not remotely terminable by an admin; they end at inactivity.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API organisation settings endpoint and Activity Feed expose effective settings and admin actions to posture tooling; server-managed settings are readable by Owners

steps.title: Read effective settings programmatically
body: Use the Compliance API directory endpoints (organizations, users, roles, groups and each organisation's effective settings) with a Compliance Access Key to evidence the configuration.

tools.name: Claude Cowork

variants.name: Cowork in Claude Desktop (local session in the Cowork VM sandbox)
Cowork in the cloud (web, mobile, Chrome side panel; sessions on Anthropic servers)
variants.note: Announced 7 July 2026 (beta, Max first). "Run Cowork in the cloud" is on by default on Team and off by default on Enterprise until 10 September 2026. Device managed settings do not reach these sessions.

variants.name: Dispatch (background tasks) and scheduled tasks

summary: Cowork is Anthropic's agentic workspace for non-developers: the Claude Code architecture inside Claude Desktop, working on the user's own files, connectors, skills and plugins, with sub-agents, browser use (Claude in Chrome or a built-in browser) and computer use. Local sessions run shell and document tools in a hardened VM on the device with file access scoped to connected folders and web fetches to an egress allowlist; cloud sessions (web, mobile, Chrome side panel) run on Anthropic's servers, save sessions and files to the account, keep working with every device offline, and can only touch local folders while the desktop app is open. Inference is the Anthropic API on first-party plans, or the organisation's provider on Claude Desktop on 3P.

Modelling it as a personal autonomous agent is a stretch in one direction (it is a vendor-managed app, not a self-hosted agent) and apt in another (it acts with the user's own folders, connectors and browser sessions). Admin control is in the claude.ai console at Organization settings > Cowork: "Enable for your organization", "Run Cowork in the cloud", the built-in browser toggle, "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode", "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools", an OTLP collector for session events, and required or hidden plugin marketplaces, with role-based access on Enterprise; on the device, Claude Desktop's managed configuration (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude) adds allowedWorkspaceFolders, coworkEgressAllowedHosts, disabledBuiltinTools, disableBypassPermissionsMode and coworkTabEnabled. Cowork sessions never fetch Claude Code server-managed settings.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise in Claude Desktop; web and mobile in beta for Pro, Max and Team and for Enterprise where admins enable it; Claude Desktop on 3P runs Cowork on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a gateway.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API (first-party) or the provider configured in Claude Desktop managed configuration (inferenceProvider gateway / bedrock / vertex / foundry / anthropic) on 3P deployments.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, the contents of files in connected folders that Claude reads, tool outputs, browser page content and connector data go to the model provider; cloud sessions store sessions and files in the account; the OTLP exporter (inside the VM, subject to egress rules) sends events to the organisation's collector.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Local conversation history stays on the device outside standard retention (Compliance API captures local sessions server-side for 6 years or the custom period); cloud sessions are saved to the account (remote transcripts 6 years unless deleted). Cowork is not covered by ZDR. Commercial terms: no training.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: claude.com/docs/cowork plus the Help Center Cowork on Team and Enterprise article

riskNotes.note: Cowork reads documents, web pages (via the built-in browser or Claude in Chrome) and connector results as instructions with "Automatically approve" on by default; the egress allowlist and connector tool approvals are the containment.
"Always allow" for connector tools is off by default because it removes the per-tool prompt; bypass permissions mode can be removed with disableBypassPermissionsMode in managed configuration.

Users can attach home folders, Documents, AppData and whole drives (September 2026); allowedWorkspaceFolders in managed configuration is the fence. OTLP export includes user prompts by default on the Team/Enterprise console integration.

Cloud sessions, Dispatch and scheduled tasks run unattended without a device; the Enterprise console can enable cloud capability per group, and the Compliance API lists remote Cowork sessions including agent-owned scheduled runs.
Users can add plugin marketplaces by URL and upload plugins; admins curate marketplaces (required, auto-installed, available, hidden) and can disable user marketplaces and uploads.

controls.mechanism: Auto-mode classifier ("Automatically approve"), browser safety classifiers, egress allowlist; Enterprise Inference hooks govern Cowork prompts

steps.title: Keep tool approvals in the loop
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off and consider turning off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions for sensitive teams.

steps.title: Inspect prompts inline (Enterprise, beta)
body: Inference hooks send every governed Cowork prompt, including tool results, to your AI security server for an allow/deny verdict before inference.

controls.mechanism: "Enable for your organization" toggle at Organization settings > Cowork; Enterprise custom roles and groups gate Cowork and cloud capability; SSO/SCIM at the organisation; forceLoginOrgUUID in Claude Desktop managed configuration

steps.title: Enable Cowork for the right people
body: Turn on "Enable for your organization" at Organization settings > Cowork and, on Enterprise, grant Cowork and cloud sessions to specific groups through custom roles.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop profile or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude so the app only accepts your organisation's logins.

controls.mechanism: Managed configuration disabledBuiltinTools (tool or argument-scoped rules such as Read(**/.env)) and builtinToolPolicy (ask / allow per tool); Claude Code managed deny rules apply to Cowork's mcp__workspace__bash and web_fetch tools in local sessions

steps.title: Deny tools by policy on the device
body: Set disabledBuiltinTools (for example Bash, Read(**/.env)) and builtinToolPolicy ask entries in Claude Desktop managed configuration; managed Bash and WebFetch deny rules in Claude Code policy also stop Cowork's workspace tools.

controls.note: Cloud sessions do not read device policy; only the console toggles and connector tool settings reach them.

controls.mechanism: TLS to the provider; egressProxyUrl / egressProxyPacUrl and mTLS variables read only from managed settings and user settings in app-managed sessions

steps.title: Pin the proxy path from managed settings
body: Deliver HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT/KEY through managed settings; Cowork sessions ignore these in repository settings so a checked-out repo cannot redirect the TLS path.

controls.mechanism: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays for local transcripts; cloud sessions deletable by users; Compliance API retention follows custom periods; skills and memory managed in Customize

steps.title: Bound local transcripts
body: Set desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays in managed settings; Desktop and Cowork transcripts are otherwise exempt from cleanupPeriodDays.

controls.mechanism: Local tools run in the hardened Cowork VM with file access scoped to connected folders (allowedWorkspaceFolders) and web fetches to coworkEgressAllowedHosts; cloud sessions run on Anthropic-managed servers; requireCoworkFullVmSandbox is deprecated

steps.title: Restrict which folders Cowork can mount
body: Set allowedWorkspaceFolders in Claude Desktop managed configuration (unset means unrestricted); September 2026 builds let users attach home folders and whole drives otherwise.

steps.title: Note the VM policy gap
body: In a full VM sandbox the device's MDM policy and managed-settings.json are not present, and Cowork never fetches server-managed settings; deliver Cowork controls through Claude Desktop managed configuration instead.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool permissions (read vs write) set org-wide at Organization settings > Connectors; "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off by default; disabledBuiltinTools and builtinToolPolicy on the device; browser toggles

steps.title: Limit connector actions organisation-wide
body: At Organization settings > Connectors restrict each connector's tools (for example search but not send) and keep "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off so each call still prompts.

steps.title: Decide on browsers
body: Toggle the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork and Claude in Chrome at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome (both off by default on Enterprise until 10 September 2026).

controls.mechanism: Enterprise-managed connector authorisation through the IdP with per-role permission scoping; otherwise Claude acts with the user's own connector and browser sessions

steps.title: Provision connectors centrally with scoped permissions

controls.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens held by the platform; inferenceCredentialHelper and credential-helper TTLs on 3P deployments; OTLP headers encrypted at rest on Anthropic servers

steps.title: Use a credential helper on third-party deployments

controls.mechanism: Organisation model restrictions and effort caps (enforced across most products), browser safety classifiers, organizationInstructions appended to the system prompt on 3P

steps.title: Restrict models and effort for Cowork users

controls.mechanism: Org-enabled connectors only (Organization settings > Connectors), desktop extension allowlist, isLocalDevMcpEnabled, managedMcpServers, admin-curated plugin marketplaces (required / auto-installed / available / hidden), userPluginMarketplacesEnabled and userPluginUploadsEnabled

steps.title: Curate plugins and marketplaces
body: Configure organisation plugin marketplaces with installation tiers under Organization settings and, on the device, set userPluginMarketplacesEnabled and userPluginUploadsEnabled false to stop users adding sources.

steps.title: Control local MCP and extensions
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false and turn on the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop) so only approved .mcpb extensions load.

controls.mechanism: Per-tool approval prompts for connector tools, "Automatically approve" (classifier) and manual modes, browser Manually approve mode, disableBypassPermissionsMode on the device

steps.title: Remove bypass and keep prompts

controls.mechanism: Organisation, group and per-user usage limits (Organization settings > Usage) shared across Cowork, Claude Code and chat; no per-task budget

steps.title: Set consumption limits
body: Configure org, group and user limits under Organization settings > Usage; user limits override group limits and the org limit is the ceiling.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry export configured at Admin settings > Cowork (OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers) with user_prompt, tool_result (decision_type, decision_source), api_request and tool_decision events carrying user.email; Compliance API local and remote Cowork session transcripts (Enterprise)

steps.title: Stream Cowork events to the SIEM
body: At Admin settings > Cowork set the OTLP endpoint, protocol and headers; events include prompts by default, so filter at the collector if needed.

steps.title: Retrieve transcripts after the fact
body: Enterprise Compliance Access Keys with read:compliance_user_data list cowork and cowork_remote sessions and return prompts, responses, tool calls and results.

controls.mechanism: Org toggle off, "Run Cowork in the cloud" off, role removal, coworkTabEnabled / secureVmFeaturesEnabled false on the device, connector disable revokes access for everyone

steps.title: Disable Cowork or its cloud variant
body: Turn off "Enable for your organization" or "Run Cowork in the cloud" at Organization settings > Cowork; on managed devices set coworkTabEnabled false.

controls.mechanism: Tenant-restriction header on claude.ai traffic; Compliance API session listing shows who is running Cowork; MDM inventory of Claude Desktop

steps.title: Block personal-account Cowork on the corporate network
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the TLS-inspecting proxy for claude.ai and api.anthropic.com.

controls.mechanism: Claude Desktop is an MDM-deployed app (PKG / MSIX); the Cowork VM is opaque to host sensors; OTLP tool_result events carry file paths and commands for the SIEM

steps.title: Use the OTLP feed as the endpoint signal
body: Enable toolDetails content capture so tool_input (paths, commands, URLs) reaches the collector, since host EDR cannot see inside the Cowork VM.

controls.note: No baseline or drift detection is offered; build it on the OTLP event stream if required.

controls.mechanism: allowedWorkspaceFolders and Read deny rules limit what can be read; connector write permissions can be removed; Inference hooks (Enterprise) inspect prompts inline; coworkEgressAllowedHosts limits where data can go

steps.title: Fence data paths
body: Combine allowedWorkspaceFolders, disabledBuiltinTools Read rules for secret paths and connector read-only permissions; add Inference hooks for inline DLP on Enterprise.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API remote session list identifies user-owned and agent-owned (scheduled) Cowork sessions; admin console shows enabled connectors, plugins and roles

steps.title: List unattended sessions
body: Query /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote; agent-owned sessions carry agent_id and started_by_user for scheduled tasks.

controls.mechanism: coworkEgressAllowedHosts (managed configuration) and the Admin settings > Capabilities > Network egress allowlist; the OTLP collector host is added automatically; egressProxyUrl for the app

controls.note: Not applicable: no model artifacts run locally; inference is remote.

summary: Anthropic's chat surfaces: claude.ai in the browser, the mobile apps, and Claude Desktop with its Chat, Cowork and Code tabs. Chat runs on the Anthropic API under the user's organisation login; connectors (MCP) reach Google Drive, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Slack and custom remote servers through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com; desktop extensions (.mcpb) and local MCP servers add device-side tools. Prompts, uploads and connector results go to Anthropic; Team and Enterprise data is not used for training and follows the organisation's retention setting (indefinite by default until a custom period is set).

Team and Enterprise administration is in the claude.ai console: SSO (SAML/OIDC via WorkOS) with domain verification and "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups gating Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag and models, connector enablement and per-tool read/write restrictions, enterprise-managed connector authorisation through the IdP, the desktop extension allowlist, audit logs (180-day export) and the Compliance API (Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, session transcripts, effective settings), custom retention, spend limits, IP allowlisting, CMEK and US-only inference. Enterprise installers deploy via Jamf, Kandji, Intune, SCCM or GPO with device policies in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude covering extensions, local MCP, Claude Code and Cowork tabs, auto-updates and forced org login; device policy overrides the in-console allowlist.

facts.value: Free, Pro, Max (consumer terms); Team (SSO, server-managed settings, analytics); Enterprise (SCIM, custom roles, Compliance API, audit logs, custom retention, CMEK, IP allowlisting, ZDR for Claude Code, HIPAA-ready option, US-only inference).

facts.value: Prompts, attachments, artifact content and connector retrievals to Anthropic; the desktop app also loads application code from claude.ai and *.claudeusercontent.com CDN hosts; the tenant-restrictions header and IP allowlist are the network-side gates.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial plans: no training; chat and project retention indefinite by default, configurable from 30 days at Organization settings > Data and privacy; audit logs 180 days; Compliance API local/remote session transcripts 6 years or the custom period.

items.title: Managed deployment and device policies
body: Device policies live in the macOS configuration-profile domain com.anthropic.claudefordesktop and the Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude registry key (HKCU is ignored when HKLM exists). The keys that matter for control: isDesktopExtensionEnabled and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled (kill switches for extensions and the directory), isLocalDevMcpEnabled (local MCP server connections), isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled, secureVmFeaturesEnabled (Cowork access), forceLoginOrgUUID, allowedWorkspaceFolders, effortLevel, disableAutoUpdates and autoUpdaterEnforcementHours. Device-level policy overrides the in-app allowlist.

Claude Desktop on 3P extends the same stores with inferenceProvider and credential keys, disabledBuiltinTools, builtinToolPolicy, disableBypassPermissionsMode, coworkEgressAllowedHosts, managedMcpServers, allowedPluginMarketplaces, userPluginMarketplacesEnabled / userPluginUploadsEnabled, sshHostAllowlist, egressProxyUrl and OTLP telemetry keys; a Linux /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json uses native JSON.

links.title: Claude Desktop configuration reference (3P managed keys)

items.title: Extension allowlist and managed connector authorization
body: Team and Enterprise Owners can turn on the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop). It ships disabled — every extension is available until it is enabled — and enabling it force-deletes existing non-allowlisted installs; custom org-scoped extensions upload in .mcpb format. Enterprise-managed connector authorization (GA) lets admins provision MCP connectors org-wide through the IdP (Okta today), assign them by role and scope the permissions Claude may request; Owners can also restrict each connector's tools to read-only and block verified-domain services from connecting to outside accounts.

items.title: Identity, audit and compliance for the organisation
body: SSO via WorkOS (Okta, Entra ID, Google, OneLogin, JumpCloud, Duo SAML) with "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping and automatic removal; Enterprise custom roles and groups; IP allowlisting (CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support); tenant restrictions via the proxy-injected anthropic-allowed-org-ids header.

Audit logs (Enterprise, 180 days, CSV by email) from Organization settings > Data and privacy; the Compliance API for the Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, directory, effective settings and Cowork / Claude Code / M365 session transcripts; custom data retention from 30 days; Inference hooks (beta) for inline allow/deny of every governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code.

links.title: Set up JIT or SCIM provisioning

riskNotes.note: Chat and project retention is indefinite until an Owner sets a period; uploads, connector results and artifacts persist with the chat. Custom retention and the Compliance API delete endpoints are the levers.

Custom remote MCP connectors and desktop extensions are user-addable by default; the extension allowlist ships disabled and Anthropic reviews Directory connectors against listing criteria without auditing them.

Connectors act with the user's granted scopes; org-wide tool restrictions (read vs write) and managed authorisation scoping keep Claude from sending mail or writing tickets when only reading is intended.
Personal accounts on the corporate network are blocked only by tenant restrictions or IP allowlisting; domain capture and SSO enforcement pull verified-domain users into the organisation.

summary: Office add-ins served from pivot.claude.ai inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook that read and write the open file or mail thread, with connectors, skills and an optional cross-app mode. Users sign in with their Claude account (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and requests go to Anthropic, or the add-in is pointed at the organisation's Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or gateway endpoint. Chat history, uploaded skills, connector registrations and the sign-in credential live in the Office webview's browser storage on each device; Anthropic deletes inputs and outputs from its backend within 30 days.

Admins deploy and gate the add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and toggle "Let Claude work across apps" at Organization settings > Office agents. Governance gaps are explicit in the docs: the add-ins do not inherit custom data retention, activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports, and Compliance API transcript coverage (office_agents/* local sessions) is in beta. A custom OpenTelemetry collector receives the full unfiltered audit trail (prompts, tool inputs and outputs, document references) from each user's browser and must support CORS.

facts.label: Inference & routing

facts.value: Backend inputs and outputs deleted within 30 days; local history keeps the 50 most recent conversations per user, organisation and app with no admin retention window; not ZDR-eligible (Claude for Excel); commercial terms, no training.

The add-in sends the open document, workbook or thread content the user asks about; Outlook requires Graph consent, and cross-app mode links context across Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook sessions.
History is keyed to a Claude account or a hashed Entra object ID; Office builds without nested app authentication fall back to a per-installation identifier shared by everyone on the device.
Add-ins can be installed from AppSource by users unless the M365 Admin Center restricts them; activity is absent from Enterprise audit logs and exports.

controls.mechanism: Trust Center first-party and third-party architecture overviews for Claude for Excel, PowerPoint, Word
