tools.name: GitHub Copilot Chat on github.com

variants.name: Copilot Chat on github.com (immersive and panel)
Copilot Chat in GitHub Mobile
Copilot Spaces (curated context, organisation-owned or personal)
Copilot Memory (public preview; used by cloud agent, code review and CLI)

summary: Copilot Chat on github.com and Mobile answers over repositories, issues and PRs the user can see, attaches images and PDFs, searches the web when the policy allows, and calls a fixed GitHub MCP server to do a limited set of tasks (branches, merges) on request; a chat can hand off into a cloud agent session. Spaces bundle repositories, files, issues and uploads as reusable context; Memory keeps repository facts and user preferences for the agents.

Inference runs on the Copilot API with enterprise-enabled models; retrieval runs with the user's own permissions (viewers of a Space only see sources they can access). Conversations are stored by GitHub: today 100 conversations with 28-day message retention, moving to life-of-account on or after 2026-09-28 when chat, Mobile chat and the cloud agent merge under one policy. Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training.

Admin levers are the "Copilot in GitHub.com" policy (soon the unified policy), the web search, Memory and models policies, content exclusion, and administrator export / delete of Memory. Spaces have no dedicated policy on the pages fetched; the MCP policy does not apply to Chat in GitHub.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All plans; Business and Enterprise gate it with Copilot in GitHub.com and, from 2026-09-28, a single policy shared with Mobile chat and the cloud agent.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API; models selectable per conversation within the enterprise Configure models policy; enterprise BYOK custom models appear in Chat; data-resident routing under the data residency policy.

facts.label: Data leaving the browser
facts.value: Prompts, attached files, repository context and (when enabled) web search results to the Copilot API; nothing runs on the device.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Up to 100 recent conversations, messages kept 28 days — changing to retention for the life of the account on or after 2026-09-28; Memory entries expire after 28 days unused; Business and Enterprise data is not used for training.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot Chat concepts, Spaces and Memory.

items.title: Policies that reach chat on github.com
body: Copilot in GitHub.com (feature toggle; opt-in preview features and feedback collection hang off it), Copilot can search the web, Configure models and Configure custom models, Copilot Memory, content exclusion — all honoured by Chat in GitHub per the supported-surfaces table. MCP servers in Copilot and the registry restriction are not: chat's GitHub MCP server is fixed. Across a user's organisations the least restrictive setting wins for most policies, but web search and public-code matching follow the most restrictive.

items.title: Memory administration and the 2026-09-28 change
body: Copilot Memory is enabled per user under an enterprise or organisation policy; admins export (JSONL) or delete user-level preferences per user or in bulk from Organization Settings > Copilot > Access or the enterprise licensing page. Memory does not apply to IDEs or the Copilot app. From 2026-09-28 chat retention becomes life-of-account; administrators who do not confirm the unified policy lose Copilot on github.com and Mobile for their users.

links.title: Managing Copilot Memory for an organisation or enterprise
Upcoming changes to Copilot policies and billing

riskNotes.note: CamoLeak (2025) turned hidden PR-description comments into silent exfiltration through GitHub's own Camo image proxy; the fix was to stop rendering images in chat. Chat still reads every issue and PR the user can see, and can now act through the GitHub MCP server.

Retention moves from 28 days to life-of-account on 2026-09-28; Spaces accept uploads and free text that are then shareable to organisation members or publicly; Memory quotes users' own words back into other sessions.
Web search and image/PDF attachments widen the inference input beyond repository data; both are policy-controlled (web search) or user-controlled (attachments) rather than inspected.
Spaces and Memory are the retrieval stores; anyone with editor access to an organisation Space, or push access to a repository, can shape what the model reads.

controls.mechanism: Copilot seat assignment (enterprise teams, IdP-synced under EMU), Copilot in GitHub.com policy, SAML SSO

steps.title: Assign seats and enable the feature
body: Grant licences from Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot (users, enterprise teams or organisations); enable Copilot in GitHub.com under AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients.

steps.title: Confirm the unified policy before 2026-09-28
body: Review the single policy replacing Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in Mobile and the cloud agent; opting out removes chat on github.com and Mobile.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; github.com chat traffic is ordinary HTTPS to github.com
controls.note: An SSE or CASB can only see the browser session; the model traffic originates from GitHub's side. Tenancy enforcement must rely on SSO and seat assignment.

controls.mechanism: Content exclusion (honoured by Chat on GitHub and Mobile) and the web-search policy; no inspection of prompts or uploads

steps.title: Exclude sensitive paths at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion: fnmatch patterns per repository or "*" — applied to chat on the GitHub website and Mobile, not to third-party agents.

steps.title: Decide on web search
body: Set Copilot can search the web at enterprise level; it is one of the policies where the most restrictive organisation setting wins.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; paste and upload controls belong to a browser security product
controls.note: Chat accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC and HEIF attachments; only a browser control can stop uploads of classified documents.

controls.mechanism: Web-search policy; image rendering disabled in chat (post-CamoLeak); GitHub MCP server limited to a fixed task set
controls.note: The model's reach is GitHub data plus web search; there is no domain allowlist for chat, and the vendor's remaining lever is to keep web search off.

steps.title: Turn web search off where exfiltration risk matters
body: Disable Copilot can search the web; it applies to IDEs and Chat in GitHub.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise AI controls tab (features, privacy, models, Memory, MCP), audit log for policy changes
controls.note: Switches and evidence of switching exist; catalogue and intake are external.

steps.title: Manage policies from the AI controls tab
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients holds the chat-relevant policies; organisation settings sit under Settings > Code, planning, and automation > Copilot.

controls.mechanism: GitHub MCP actions run "at your request" in the conversation; agent hand-offs land in the cloud agent's draft-PR and workflow-approval gates
controls.note: The chat page documents no per-action approval prompt for the built-in MCP tasks; the human gate is the conversation itself and, downstream, PR review.

steps.title: Keep the downstream gates
body: Chat can create branches or merge PRs on request and can start cloud agent sessions; branch protections, rulesets and workflow approval remain the enforced approvals.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-side mitigations (image rendering disabled after CamoLeak; hidden-character filtering for agent hand-offs); no customer configuration

steps.title: Know what the vendor changed
body: Image rendering in Copilot Chat was disabled on 2025-08-14 to close the Camo exfiltration channel; hidden HTML comments in issues and PRs are filtered before agent prompts.

controls.mechanism: Chat acts as the signed-in user; there is no separate agent identity to manage
controls.note: Actions taken through chat's GitHub MCP server are the user's own; attribution is the user account.

controls.mechanism: Policy state is visible in the UI and audit log; an SSPM tool reads it via the audit log stream and REST APIs
Conversation retention (28 days → life of account from 2026-09-28), Memory export / delete and 28-day expiry, Spaces visibility settings

steps.title: Export or delete Memory when required
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Access: Export Copilot memories / Delete Copilot memories per user, or Download / Delete user memories in bulk (JSONL, 10 exports per hour).

steps.title: Plan for life-of-account chat retention
body: After 2026-09-28 chat conversations are retained for the life of the account rather than 28 days; treat chat history as a data store in retention policy.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; model-hosting page lists providers and retention terms

steps.title: Record the provider set
body: OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS / Anthropic / GCP (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default), Google, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry / Fireworks.

controls.mechanism: No customer-managed keys; regional routing via the data residency policy
controls.note: "Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models" (off by default, +10% credits) keeps inference in the US or EU boundary; keys remain GitHub's.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable — chat holds no agent credentials; secret scanning covers repository content, not chat uploads
controls.note: Uploaded files and pasted text are not secret-scanned; content exclusion of secret paths is the only vendor lever.

controls.mechanism: Fixed GitHub MCP server with a limited task set; MCP policy and registry restriction do not apply to Chat in GitHub; web-search policy
controls.note: The tool set cannot be narrowed by the customer; only web search can be switched off.

steps.title: Accept the fixed tool set or disable the surface
body: The supported-surfaces table shows MCP servers in Copilot as not applicable to Copilot Chat in GitHub; the built-in GitHub MCP server performs a limited set of tasks at the user's request.

controls.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user; Space viewers only see sources they have access to; no remediation of over-shared repositories

steps.title: Rely on repository permissions and Space visibility
body: Organisation-owned Spaces grant admin / editor / viewer or No access; viewers only see sources they can already access — fix repository over-sharing first.

controls.mechanism: Organisation-owned Spaces with role-based sharing; enterprise custom agents and the Agent apps policy; no registry for Spaces
controls.note: Anyone with a Copilot licence, including Free, can create a Space; there is no dedicated Spaces policy on the pages fetched — only visibility settings per Space.

steps.title: Prefer organisation-owned Spaces
body: Create shared Spaces under the organisation so access is admin / editor / viewer by member rather than public or user-by-user.

controls.mechanism: Audit log records policy, licensing and Memory administration events (180 days, streamable); chat prompts are not logged

steps.title: Stream policy and licensing events
body: Filter action:copilot in the enterprise audit log and stream to a SIEM; client and chat prompts are not recorded.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; personal Copilot accounts on github.com are invisible to the enterprise
Copilot in GitHub.com policy Disabled everywhere (unified policy from 2026-09-28); seat removal; Memory policy Disabled everywhere with bulk delete

steps.title: Disable at enterprise scope
body: Set Copilot in GitHub.com to Disabled everywhere; across enterprises the most restrictive policy applies, within one enterprise set it at enterprise level.

steps.title: Purge Memory
body: Set Copilot Memory to Disabled everywhere and use Delete user memories in bulk.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot CLI

variants.name: Copilot CLI (GA 2026-02-25)
GitHub Copilot app (desktop, GA 2026-06-17; same managed-settings plane, own policy since 2026-07-27)
Copilot in Windows Terminal (Canary; governed by the Copilot CLI policy)

summary: Copilot CLI is the terminal-native coding agent (plan mode, autopilot, built-in Explore / Task / Code Review / Plan agents, /fleet parallel sessions, hooks, plugins, MCP) and the runtime behind the GitHub Copilot desktop app, the SDK and JetBrains agent mode. It runs on the developer's machine with the developer's GitHub identity; inference goes to the Copilot API by plan, or straight to a provider under local BYOK.

Prompts, file contents and tool output leave the device for the Copilot API; session data (prompts, responses, tools, files changed) is written to ~/.copilot/session-state and, by default, synced to the user's GitHub account under the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy. Remote steering exposes the session to github.com and GitHub Mobile. Nothing reaches the organisation's audit log except policy changes.

The admin plane is managed-settings.json: server-managed from the .github-private repository (copilot/managed-settings.json, with team overrides), MDM (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot, com.github.copilot) or a root-owned file. It carries deny / ask / allow permissions with Shell, Read, Edit and Domain selectors (GA 2026-09-09), disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, plugin marketplaces, the MXC local sandbox policy, OpenTelemetry export and remote-control mode.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise gate it with the Copilot CLI policy (Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients), and the desktop app with its own GitHub Copilot app policy.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API per plan; enterprise-enabled models only; local BYOK (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Ollama) bypasses GitHub; enterprise BYOK models are served by the Copilot API.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts and tool output to the Copilot API; session data synced to the GitHub account unless remoteExport is false; OTLP telemetry only where the enterprise configures it; remote-steering traffic to github.com.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under ZDR except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 (retain by default, exemption available through end-2026).

facts.label: Sandboxes
facts.value: Local sandbox uses Microsoft eXecution Container (MXC: Seatbelt on macOS 15+, bubblewrap on Linux, BaseContainer on Windows 11); cloud sandbox runs on Azure Container Apps Sandboxes behind the Cloud sandbox access policy (off by default). Both public preview.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot CLI how-tos (install, authenticate, allowing tools, hooks, MCP, plugins, administer for your enterprise).

items.title: Managed settings — delivery and precedence
body: Server-managed: an organisation in the enterprise hosts .github-private with copilot/managed-settings.json (legacy .github/copilot/settings.json still read); copilot/team-mappings.json and copilot/teams/*.json let named teams relax keys the enterprise marks { "overridable": ... }. Clients refresh within about an hour, or on restart. MDM and local-file delivery exist for machines that must not depend on the server channel; the CLI falls back to its cached copy when a fetch fails.

Keys the CLI honours: permissions.deny / ask / allow, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, model, enabledPlugins / extraKnownMarketplaces / strictKnownMarketplaces, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, telemetry.*, remoteControl and sandbox.* — sandbox is CLI-only, the app ignores telemetry, the cloud agent honours only model and plugin keys.

items.title: Permission model and its escape hatches
body: Read-only operations run without asking; edits, destructive shell commands and URL fetches prompt. Per-repo approvals persist in ~/.copilot/permissions-config.json and allowed URLs in ~/.copilot/settings.json. --allow-all / --yolo, /allow-all, --allow-all-tools and autopilot remove the prompts; deny rules still win. The managed file removes these options with disableBypassPermissionsMode and pins its own deny / ask / allow.

Policy hooks — root-owned, machine-wide, immune to disableAllHooks — run preToolUse (fail-closed on error, fail-open on timeout) and permissionRequest with a permissionDecision of allow, deny or ask; HTTP hooks for those events must be https.

items.title: Local sandbox policy
body: Deny-by-default filesystem: read/write, read-only and denied paths, with automatic grants for the working directory, PATH toolchains and package caches that managed settings can switch off (addCurrentWorkingDirectory, allowDevToolAccess). Network allowOutbound / allowLocalNetwork and an HTTP proxy; gitAuth / ghAuth token injection and macOS keychainAccess are separate switches. Managed values combine in the most restrictive direction; built-in file tools are software-checked only and remote MCP servers are outside the policy.

links.title: Understanding filesystem policies for local sandboxing

riskNotes.note: Autopilot and --yolo exist by design; CVE-2026-29783 showed the read-only classifier itself could be tricked by bash parameter expansion. disableBypassPermissionsMode plus a managed sandbox is the only configuration where a bad tool call is contained rather than merely prompted.

Repository files, MCP responses and hook output all feed the agent; the vendor's fix for CVE-2026-29783 added parse-time blocking and prompt hardening but no classifier. Domain() deny rules and sandbox allowOutbound=false bound the exfiltration path.

Session transcripts sync to github.com by default and remote steering publishes them to the agents list; OTLP captureContent can also carry prompts. Decide the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy and lockCaptureContent explicitly.

Plugins and MCP servers install by name from marketplaces and npx commands; only strictKnownMarketplaces and the managed allowlist (URL and stdio command match) bound the sources — the registry restriction is name-only and bypassable.

controls.mechanism: Copilot seat plus the Copilot CLI policy (and the separate GitHub Copilot app policy); OAuth device/browser flow or a fine-grained PAT with the Copilot Requests permission; SAML SSO authorisation per organisation

steps.title: Enable the CLI for the right organisations
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients: set Copilot CLI to Enabled everywhere, Disabled everywhere or Let organizations decide; users still need an assigned seat.

steps.title: Set the desktop app policy separately
body: Since 2026-07-27 the GitHub Copilot app has its own policy under AI Controls > Copilot Clients (default Enabled everywhere); it no longer follows the CLI policy.

steps.title: Constrain how the CLI authenticates
body: OAuth tokens (gho_) and fine-grained PATs (github_pat_, Copilot Requests permission) are accepted; classic PATs are not. Tokens live in the OS keychain with a plaintext fallback at ~/.copilot/config.json; SSO-protected organisations require Authorize at login.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(), Read(), Edit(), Domain() selectors (GA 2026-09-09); root-owned policy hooks on preToolUse / permissionRequest

steps.title: Write the managed permission rules
body: Under permissions set deny (blocked from any source), ask (fresh approval every time, bypass cannot satisfy) and allow (intersection across sources) with Shell(...) / Bash(...) / PowerShell(...), Read(path), Edit(path) / Write(path) and Domain(host) selectors; mark team-relaxable keys { "overridable": ... }.

steps.title: Add a machine-wide policy hook
body: Deploy a root-owned policy hook file; a preToolUse hook returning permissionDecision "deny" blocks the call, errors and exit code 2 deny (fail-closed), timeouts fail open — set timeoutSec accordingly. disableAllHooks cannot switch policy hooks off.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; model-hosting page and provider ZDR terms are the assessment inputs
controls.note: Local BYOK changes the subprocessor set per developer — disable it through the "Configure custom models" policy if the vendor assessment did not cover the providers.

steps.title: Record model providers and retention terms
body: Enumerate hosting per model (Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, GCP, xAI, Fireworks) and the Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retention exception.

controls.mechanism: Content exclusion applies to the CLI and the app; Read() deny rules and sandbox deniedPaths keep files out of tools; telemetry.captureContent=false with lockCaptureContent
controls.note: A context filter and path denies, not inspection: nothing scans the prompt stream for sensitive content, and the model still sees whatever the developer pastes.

steps.title: Deny secret paths to the agent's tools
body: Put Read(**/.env) and similar under permissions.deny; add the same paths to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths, which managed values add to rather than replace.

steps.title: Apply content exclusion and lock telemetry content
body: Enterprise and organisation content-exclusion rules apply to the CLI ("Excluded files are not used as context"); set telemetry.captureContent=false and lockCaptureContent=true so exports never carry prompts.

controls.mechanism: permissions.deny / allow selectors, disableBypassPermissionsMode, --available-tools / --excluded-tools, MCP tool-level selectors such as MyMCP(create_issue)

steps.title: Remove the all-tools switches
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable": --yolo, --allow-all and /allow-all are suppressed and autopilot cannot skip approvals.

steps.title: Scope shell, write and MCP tools
body: Use shell(git:*), write(path) and MyMCP(tool) selectors in --allow-tool / --deny-tool or the managed rules; --available-tools restricts the agent to a named set and deny always beats allow, even under --allow-all.

controls.mechanism: managed sandbox.* keys (enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowBypass, sandboxMcpServers, sandboxLspServers, userPolicy.filesystem / network / seatbelt); Cloud sandbox access policy
controls.note: Public preview; requires macOS 15+, bubblewrap 0.5+ or recent Windows 11. Remote MCP servers and the built-in file tools sit outside the OS enforcement.

steps.title: Make the local sandbox mandatory
body: Set sandbox.enabled=true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true and sandbox.allowBypass=false so /sandbox disable, --no-sandbox and per-command bypass requests are refused; add sandboxMcpServers and sandboxLspServers=true.

steps.title: Narrow the filesystem and network policy
body: Set addCurrentWorkingDirectory and allowDevToolAccess as needed, pin userPolicy.filesystem readwritePaths / readonlyPaths / deniedPaths, and set userPolicy.network.allowOutbound and allowLocalNetwork; verify with /sandbox policy.

steps.title: Decide on cloud sandboxes
body: Enterprise > Policies > Sandboxes > Cloud sandbox access is Disabled by default; choose Let organizations enable or Enabled by default. Cloud sessions run on GitHub-hosted Azure Container Apps Sandboxes and are usage-billed.

controls.mechanism: sandbox.gitAuth / ghAuth / seatbelt.keychainAccess=false stop the developer's tokens reaching sandboxed commands; fine-grained PATs with only Copilot Requests for automation

steps.title: Stop token injection into sandboxed commands
body: Set sandbox.gitAuth=false and sandbox.ghAuth=false so the GitHub token is not exported into git HTTPS or gh inside the sandbox, and seatbelt.keychainAccess=false on macOS.

steps.title: Use narrow tokens for headless runs
body: For CI or scripted use pass COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN as a fine-grained PAT with only the Copilot Requests account permission rather than the developer's OAuth token.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (repository facts and user preferences, 28-day unused expiry, admin export / delete); "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy and remoteExport
controls.note: Memory entries are validated against the current branch before use but there is no quarantine or rollback; an admin can only delete. The CLI uses Memory, the supported-surfaces table notwithstanding — treat the concept page as authoritative for scope.

steps.title: Set the Memory policy and keep the delete lever
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory: Enabled / Disabled / Let organizations decide. Export or delete a user's memories from Organization Settings > Copilot > Access (Export / Delete Copilot memories) or in bulk from Get usage report.

steps.title: Decide whether session transcripts leave the device

body.Sessions sync to the GitHub account by d: false, and the organisation controls availability with the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy. Enabling it does not give admins access to the data.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-side parse-time blocking of dangerous shell patterns and hardened system prompts (post CVE-2026-29783); userPromptSubmitted / preToolUse hooks; no classifier

steps.title: Keep the CLI current and add hook-based screening
body: Run >= 0.0.423 (the fix blocks ${var@P}-style expansions unconditionally); use policy hooks on userPromptSubmitted and preToolUse to screen or deny suspicious inputs and tool arguments.

controls.mechanism: OS keychain storage for the GitHub token (plaintext ~/.copilot/config.json fallback); sandbox deniedPaths and Read() deny rules for secret files; no vault integration

steps.title: Keep credentials in the keychain
body: Ensure a keychain (Keychain Access, Credential Manager, libsecret) is available; without one the token is stored in plaintext in ~/.copilot/config.json.

steps.title: Deny secret files to tools and the sandbox
body: Add .env and credential paths to permissions.deny (Read / Edit) and to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths.

controls.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (serverName, serverUrl with wildcards and canonicalisation, serverCommand exact match; fail-closed with an empty allowlist); sandboxMcpServers; registry restriction (preview, bypassable)

steps.title: Publish the allowlist and denylist
body: In copilot/managed-settings.json add allowedMcpServers (omit = allow all, [] = block all but built-ins) and deniedMcpServers (always wins); entries with unresolved variables are blocked. Prerequisites: MCP servers in Copilot enabled, registry restriction set to Allow all.

steps.title: Run local MCP servers inside the sandbox
body: Set sandbox.sandboxMcpServers=true so stdio servers inherit the filesystem and network policy; remote servers remain outside it.

steps.title: Treat the registry as discovery only
body: The custom registry (CLI 1.0.11+) shows approved servers but its Registry only mode matches by name/ID and can be bypassed by editing configuration files.

controls.mechanism: permissions.ask rules, disableBypassPermissionsMode, permissionRequest policy hook, remote steering on github.com / Mobile for out-of-terminal approval

steps.title: Force approval on privileged operations
body: Put Shell(git push*), Edit(**/.github/**) and Domain(*) style selectors under permissions.ask; ask rules need a fresh one-time approval each call and saved approvals cannot satisfy them.

steps.title: Decide who may answer prompts remotely
body: remoteControl.mode = "disabled" prevents remote steering of sessions on the device; "requireSSO" with githubDotComOrganizations limits it to SSO-authorised clients.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom agents (available to the CLI), enterprise plugin standards (enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, strictKnownMarketplaces), MCP registry
controls.note: Approved agents, plugins and servers can be published centrally; there is no inventory of what sessions actually load and no reconciliation report.

steps.title: Pin marketplaces and required plugins
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces (an empty array locks all installation), extraKnownMarketplaces with source github / git / directory, and enabledPlugins as PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE: true|false.

controls.mechanism: Managed telemetry.* OTLP export (traces, metrics, events; content off by default); enterprise audit log records only policy changes; local session store and cloud session sync
controls.note: Without an OTLP collector the only records are on the developer's disk and in their personal GitHub session history, which admins cannot read.

steps.title: Pin the OpenTelemetry export
body: Set telemetry.enabled=true, telemetry.endpoint, telemetry.protocol (http/json or http/protobuf), telemetry.headers, serviceName and resourceAttributes; enforced across clients and not user-overridable.

steps.title: Watch policy events in the audit log
body: Enterprise policy updates that affect the CLI are recorded as audit-log events (action:copilot, 180 days); client prompts are not.

controls.mechanism: No discovery feature; seat and policy gating prevent unlicensed use of the enterprise's Copilot but not personal accounts
controls.note: A developer can sign the CLI into a personal Copilot account; only an endpoint or proxy-based inventory shows that. Note that the npm package @github/copilot installs without any organisational hook.

controls.mechanism: Copilot CLI policy Disabled everywhere; GitHub Copilot app policy; seat removal; allowedMcpServers []; sandbox and permission rules refresh within an hour

steps.title: Disable the client at enterprise scope
body: Set the Copilot CLI policy (and separately the GitHub Copilot app policy) to Disabled everywhere; Windows Terminal Copilot follows the CLI policy.

steps.title: Quarantine tooling without disabling the client
body: Set allowedMcpServers to [] and strictKnownMarketplaces to [] in managed settings to cut all MCP servers and plugin installs; clients pick it up within about an hour or on restart.

controls.mechanism: None from the vendor; the MXC sandbox and root-owned policy hooks are the device-side integration points
controls.note: Policy hooks (preToolUse, permissionRequest) can call an endpoint agent over https; the OTLP export gives an EDR/XDR the session context.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom agents, custom instructions, strictKnownMarketplaces; repository .github instruction and hook files remain writable by contributors
controls.note: Repository-level instructions, skills and hooks are loaded from the checked-out tree; the CLI loads policy files before repository, user and plugin sources so a policy hook can screen them, but there is no version pin.

steps.title: Prefer enterprise custom agents and policy hooks
body: Publish enterprise custom agents (available to the CLI) and deploy machine-wide policy hooks, which load ahead of repository and user hooks.

controls.mechanism: No manifests or signatures for plugins, skills or MCP servers
controls.note: strictKnownMarketplaces and extraKnownMarketplaces.autoUpdate=false give source pinning; nothing verifies content or records versions.

controls.mechanism: Domain() deny / ask / allow managed permissions; sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound / allowLocalNetwork and HTTP proxy; documented service-domain allowlist

steps.title: Deny domains in managed permissions
body: Add Domain(...) selectors under permissions.deny (and ask for the rest); matching is host-based, case-insensitive, with *.example.com covering subdomains.

steps.title: Cut sandboxed network access
body: Set sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound=false and allowLocalNetwork=false, or route through the sandbox HTTP proxy.

steps.title: Allowlist the service domains at the perimeter
body: Permit *.githubcopilot.com with the plan-specific subdomain, the github.com login and api.github.com copilot_internal endpoints, and the Azure speech domains only if voice is used.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable to vendor-hosted models; local BYOK (Ollama and OpenAI-compatible endpoints) is outside the vendor's control
controls.note: Disable local BYOK with the "Configure custom models" policy if unscanned local models are a concern.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent

variants.name: Copilot cloud agent (formerly "coding agent") and automations
Copilot code review (agentic; PR approval in public preview since 2026-09-01)
Partner coding agents — Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex (public preview)
Agent apps (partner GitHub Apps exposing agents; "Agent apps" policy)
GitHub Agentic Workflows (public preview; markdown compiled to a hardened .lock.yml)

summary: The cloud agent takes an issue, PR comment, chat hand-off or automation trigger and works in an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment (59-minute hard limit) on a copilot/ branch, pushing a draft PR that a human must review and merge. Code review, partner agents (Claude, Codex), agent apps and Agentic Workflows run on the same Actions substrate and share its mitigations; automations re-run the agent on schedules and repository events.

Inference runs on the Copilot API against enterprise-enabled models; the runner talks to api.<plan>.githubcopilot.com behind an egress firewall that, by default, allows package registries and certificate authorities only. The GitHub MCP server is wired in with a read-only token scoped to the repository; other MCP servers run with whatever secrets the administrator places in the Agents secret type — and are used without approval prompts.

Governance is enterprise-first: AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent with Enabled for selected organisations (custom properties via REST), organisation and repository access controls, Actions workflow approval, validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency review, Copilot review), runner type and the firewall. Sessions are visible at github.com/copilot/agents and in the audit log as actor:Copilot with agent_session_id.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All paid Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise require the cloud agent policy. Billing is GitHub Actions minutes plus AI credits; organisation budgets block agent features when exhausted.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API from the Actions runner (api.business / api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); models per the enterprise Configure models policy; data-resident routing under the "Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models" policy (+10% credits). Enterprise BYOK does not apply to the cloud agent.

facts.label: Data leaving the environment
facts.value: Repository contents, issue and PR text and tool output go to the Copilot API; outbound network from Bash tools is firewalled; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps are not firewalled; session logs and commits persist on GitHub.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Ephemeral environment destroyed after the session; session logs are retained and can be archived, not deleted; Business and Enterprise data is not used for training; Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default at the provider.

facts.label: Policy change 2026-09-28
facts.value: Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in GitHub Mobile and the cloud agent merge under one policy on or after 2026-09-28; chat retention moves from 28 days to the life of the account. Admins must confirm the unified policy before that date.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Cloud agent concepts: about, risks and mitigations, MCP, automations, access management.

items.title: Enablement, targeting and repository scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: Disabled (default), Enabled for all organizations, Enabled for selected organizations (UI, or by custom property through the REST API), or let organisations decide. Organisation owners then set Repository access (all or selected repositories); owners and users can opt individual repositories out. Only users with write access can trigger the agent, and automations ignore events from users without write access by default.

Third-party agents and agent apps are separate policies: disabling the cloud agent does not disable Claude or Codex agents, and the "Agent apps" policy gates partner apps installed in the enterprise's organisations. Content exclusion does not apply to third-party agents.

links.title: Enabling the cloud agent in your enterprise
Managing access to the cloud agent

items.title: The environment — setup steps, secrets, runners, firewall
body: .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml on the default branch (job name copilot-setup-steps; only steps, permissions, runs-on, services, snapshot and timeout-minutes are honoured; 59 minutes maximum) prepares the runner. Secrets and variables come only from the Agents type (repository or organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* entries reach MCP servers only; Actions, Codespaces and Dependabot secrets are never exposed.

The firewall is on by default with a recommended allowlist (OS and language package registries, container registries, certificate authorities, Playwright browser hosts); organisations and repositories add domain or URL rules or disable it. It applies only to processes the agent starts through its Bash tools — not MCP servers, not setup steps. Blocked requests are reported in the PR body or a comment. Runners default to GitHub-hosted; larger runners and ARC-managed self-hosted runners (Ubuntu x64; never non-ARC) need api.githubcopilot.com, uploads.github.com and user-images.githubusercontent.com.

links.title: Configure secrets and variables for the cloud agent

items.title: Output controls — workflow approval, validation, code review approvals
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent: Validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency advisories, Copilot code review; on by default) and Actions workflow approval (Require approval for workflow runs; keep it on — the docs warn about auto-running workflows on agent code). The agent cannot mark a PR ready, approve or merge; rulesets add one more approval when the PR is opened under the agent's app identity, and the requesting user cannot approve their own request.

Copilot code review can be authorised to approve PRs (public preview): enterprise "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default, organisations choose whether approvals count toward merge requirements, repositories can limit that to file-path globs.

links.title: Configuring settings for the cloud agent

riskNotes.note: Every trigger is attacker-reachable text (issues, PR bodies, comments, repository files). GitHub strips hidden characters and HTML comments before prompting and ignores non-write-access events for automations, but MCP tools run without approval, so an injection that reaches a write-capable MCP tool acts immediately.

The firewall covers only Bash-spawned processes; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps have unrestricted egress, and Agents secrets are plain environment variables inside the runner. Put nothing in the Agents secret type that a compromised MCP server should not see.

Automations act under their creator's identity and cannot approve the resulting PRs; partner agents install as GitHub Apps (anthropic code agent, openai code agent) with their own permissions. Rulesets and the extra-approval rule are the boundary, not the agent.
Cloud agent, third-party agents and agent apps are three independent policies; a "disabled" cloud agent still leaves Claude, Codex and any installed agent app enabled unless each is switched off.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise policy Enabled for selected organizations (UI or custom properties via REST), organisation Repository access, per-repository opt-out; write access required to trigger

steps.title: Enable for selected organisations
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Copilot Cloud Agent: choose Enabled for selected organizations and pick organisations, or select them by custom property with the REST API.

steps.title: Scope repositories
body: Organisation owners set Repository access to all or selected repositories; repository owners can opt out. Only users with write access can trigger the agent.

controls.mechanism: The agent acts under its own app identity with signed ("Verified") commits, co-authored by the requesting human; audit events carry actor_is_agent and agent_session_id; partner agents install as named GitHub Apps
controls.note: The identity is GitHub's, not the customer's: there is no key custody or lifecycle to manage, only the app installations of partner agents and agent apps to review.

steps.title: Review partner-agent app installations
body: Enabling Claude or Codex agents installs the "anthropic code agent" / "openai code agent" GitHub Apps; their actions appear in the audit log — review installations under third-party access.

steps.title: Attribute agent actions in the audit log
body: Filter actor:Copilot; agentic events carry actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the initiating user.

controls.mechanism: Agents-type secrets and variables (repository / organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* prefix scopes values to MCP servers; no access to Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets

steps.title: Use the Agents secret type only
body: Add secrets under Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents; prefix MCP credentials COPILOT_MCP_ so they are only available to MCP server configuration and never exported as general environment variables.

steps.title: Keep engine credentials out of Agentic Workflow agents
body: In Agentic Workflows the real engine key stays in the AWF API proxy sidecar; the agent container sees only a dummy key — configure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY as repository secrets, not in the workflow body.

controls.mechanism: No customer-managed keys; the only lever is regional routing under the data residency policy
controls.note: GitHub holds keys for repository data, session logs and Agents secrets. Enable "Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models" if residency is required (+10% credits).

controls.mechanism: Enterprise-level custom agents (AI Controls, REST API), agent sessions list at github.com/copilot/agents, agent apps marketplace category
controls.note: The enterprise can publish approved custom agents and see sessions, but partner agents and agent apps are approved by policy toggle, not registered — and content exclusion and the registry restriction do not apply to them.

steps.title: Publish enterprise custom agents
body: Define custom agents at enterprise level under AI Controls or through the REST API and control who may manage them.

controls.mechanism: Organisation-by-organisation enablement (custom properties), repository access lists, Configure models policy; no versioned agent definitions
controls.note: Roll out by organisation and repository; there is no canary or rollback for the agent itself, and model deprecations are announced on the changelog rather than pinned.

steps.title: Stage by organisation and repository
body: Use Enabled for selected organizations plus Repository access lists to widen scope in steps; agent apps and partner agents are enabled separately.

controls.mechanism: MCP configuration "tools" arrays, read-only GitHub MCP token scoped to the repository, per-automation tool selection, least-privilege permissions in copilot-setup-steps, no push to default branch / no merge

steps.title: Name the tools each MCP server may expose
body: In Repository Settings > Copilot > MCP servers set "tools" to the specific tool names rather than "*"; Copilot uses configured tools autonomously and will not ask for approval.

steps.title: Pick tools per automation
body: When creating an automation choose exactly which tools it can use; Suggest tools proposes a minimal set.

steps.title: Keep setup-step permissions minimal
body: Set permissions in copilot-setup-steps.yml to the lowest needed (contents: read only if the step clones).

controls.mechanism: Human review and merge of draft PRs; Actions workflow approval; ruleset extra approval for agent-opened PRs; code review approval policy off by default

steps.title: Keep workflow approval on
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent > Actions workflow approval: leave Require approval for workflow runs enabled so a user with write access must click Approve and run workflows.

steps.title: Keep the extra approval rule and required checks
body: Rulesets require one more approval when a PR is opened under the agent's app identity (enabled by default); the requester cannot approve, and branch protections apply.

steps.title: Decide whether Copilot may approve PRs
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot code review > "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default; organisations decide whether approvals count toward merge requirements.

controls.mechanism: Hidden-character and HTML-comment stripping before prompting, automations ignore non-write events, a content safety system on prompts and responses; Agentic Workflows sanitise user content and gate writes behind a threat-detection job
controls.note: No customer-configurable classifier; the structural gates (firewall, tool selection, workflow approval) carry the weight once injection succeeds.

steps.title: Leave untrusted-event handling at its default
body: Automations ignore events from users without write access by default; do not opt in unless the tool set is read-only.

steps.title: Use Agentic Workflows for event-driven automation that must be hardened
body: Agents run read-only; writes are buffered as safe outputs, scanned by a detection job and executed by a separate job — with @mention neutralisation, size limits and min-integrity filtering of inputs.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; partner agents add Anthropic and OpenAI as processors of repository content
controls.note: The third-party agent page does not state where partner agents execute or what data reaches the partner; obtain that from the partner before enabling the policy.

steps.title: Record the partner-agent data path before enabling
body: Partner agents consume Actions minutes and AI credits and install partner GitHub Apps; the docs do not describe partner-side processing — ask the vendor.

controls.mechanism: Session logs (reasoning, tool calls, token usage) at github.com/copilot/agents and in the repository Agents tab; commit messages link to sessions; no OpenTelemetry export for the cloud agent
controls.note: Logs are queryable in the UI and streamed live, but the managed telemetry export does not cover the cloud agent, so traces cannot leave GitHub programmatically.

steps.title: Use session logs and the agents panel
body: Open github.com/copilot/agents or the repository Agents tab; each session shows internal reasoning, tools used, token usage and session length, and every agent commit links back to it.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise / organisation audit log (actor:Copilot, actor_is_agent, agent_session_id, 180 days, streaming to SIEM); signed commits with human co-author

steps.title: Stream agent audit events
body: Filter actor:Copilot for agent actions and action:copilot for policy changes; stream the enterprise audit log to a SIEM for retention beyond 180 days.

steps.title: Correlate on agent_session_id
body: Agentic events record the action, actor_is_agent=true, agent_session_id and the initiating user; available to EMU enterprises and GHEC with data residency.

controls.mechanism: Vendor safety system that scans prompts and responses for harmful, offensive or insecure content; not customer-configurable
controls.note: No denied-topic or blocked-term configuration; validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning) act on the output instead.

steps.title: Rely on the built-in filter and output validation
body: The application card describes a safety system on prompts and responses plus CodeQL, secret scanning and dependency analysis on generated code.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (public preview): repository-scoped facts validated against the current branch, user preferences owned by the billing entity, 28-day unused expiry, admin export / delete

steps.title: Set the Memory policy
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory: Enabled everywhere, Disabled everywhere or Let organizations decide.

steps.title: Know the scope and expiry
body: Repository facts stay in their repository and carry code citations; entries unused for 28 days are deleted; code review uses repository facts only.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-side evaluation (SWE-Bench, internal suites, RAI red teaming) and per-session validation tools on the output; no customer evaluation harness
controls.note: Validation tools are a release gate on each PR, not an evaluation of agent behaviour; keep them on and add your own CI checks.

steps.title: Keep validation tools enabled
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent > Validation tools: CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency advisories and Copilot code review run before the PR is handed over; disabling them speeds the agent up at the cost of the gate.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise AI controls tab (Agents, Copilot, MCP policies), Copilot usage metrics, REST API for cloud agent management
controls.note: GitHub gives the policy switches and usage data; the catalogue, intake and evidence workflow are an external governance platform's job.

steps.title: Centralise policy on the AI controls tab
body: Agents, Copilot and MCP policies live under Enterprise > AI controls; within an enterprise the least restrictive organisation setting usually wins, so set lockdowns there.

controls.mechanism: 59-minute hard session limit, organisation AI-credit budgets that block agent features when exhausted, Actions minutes, autopilot continuation limits in automations

steps.title: Set AI-credit budgets
body: When budget limits are exhausted, code reviews and other AI-credit features are blocked; enable AI credits paid usage deliberately.

steps.title: Rely on the session ceiling
body: Each cloud agent session runs at most 59 minutes and cannot be extended; setup steps share that limit.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise policy Disabled, repository opt-out, Stop session, firewall on, separate third-party and agent-app policies

steps.title: Stop a running session
body: Click Stop session in the session log viewer to end the Actions run; pushed commits are preserved.

steps.title: Disable every agent policy, not just one
body: Set Copilot Cloud Agent to Disabled, and separately disable Third-party agents and Agent apps under AI controls > Agents — disabling the cloud agent does not disable the others.

controls.mechanism: REST endpoints for cloud agent management and the audit log stream are the inputs an SSPM product would read
controls.note: No first-party posture report; poll the cloud agent management API and audit log from an SSPM tool to evidence firewall, approval and policy settings.

summary: Governance runs through the enterprise AI-controls tab and organisation Copilot settings: Feature, Privacy and Models policies set enterprise-first (enable, disable, or let organisations decide), with content exclusion and MCP governance layered on for Business and Enterprise plans.

Inference runs on GitHub's Copilot API (api.*.githubcopilot.com per plan) against models hosted on Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, GCP, xAI and Fireworks; with local BYOK the prompts go straight from the editor to the chosen provider and bypass GitHub. Prompts, open-file context, tool arguments and (in agent mode) shell output leave the device; the audit log never sees them — only an OpenTelemetry export the enterprise pins in managed settings does.

Two admin planes overlap in VS Code: device policy (Windows registry Software\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode, macOS configuration profiles, /etc/vscode/policy.json) and GitHub's managed-settings.json (MDM key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot / com.github.copilot, then server-managed copilot/managed-settings.json, then a local file). Where both set the same policy the Copilot managed setting wins. JetBrains honours the managed file for MCP, plugins, telemetry and bypass-mode lockout (2026-08-18) and a managed sandbox in preview (2026-09-08); Visual Studio is ADMX-only.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max; Business and Enterprise carry policies, content exclusion, MCP governance and managed settings.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: GitHub Copilot API by plan (*.business / *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS Bedrock / Anthropic / GCP, Gemini on GCP, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry/Fireworks. Data residency (US, EU) is a policy at +10% credits.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, file context and tool outputs to the Copilot API; telemetry to collector.github.com and copilot-telemetry.githubusercontent.com; local BYOK sends prompts directly to the provider; enterprise BYOK stays server-side.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under zero-data-retention except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1, which retain by default with a ZDR exemption available through end-2026.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: GitHub Copilot documentation, plus the VS Code enterprise policy reference.

items.title: Enterprise and organisation policy framework
body: Policies gate which Copilot features, agents and models users can access — named policies include MCP servers in Copilot, restricting MCP to registry servers, allowed models, custom models, web search, Copilot Memory and suggestions-matching-public-code (blocked by default for Business seats). Conflict rules matter for design: within one enterprise the least restrictive setting wins across a user's organisations, so a lockdown must be set at the enterprise level to be a lockdown.

items.title: MCP governance and content exclusion
body: The MCP policy gates whether MCP servers run at all across Copilot clients; server allowlisting comes in two strengths — a GitHub-hosted Managed Settings File (GA, matched on name, URL and stdio command, not user-bypassable) and a Custom MCP Registry (preview, name matching only, bypassable by editing local config). Content exclusion (Business and Enterprise) applies at repository, organisation and enterprise scope with fnmatch patterns, but is not honoured by the edit and agent modes of Chat in VS Code and other editors, nor by third-party agents — scope guidance accordingly.

items.title: Audit surface and network posture
body: The organisation audit log records Copilot licensing, settings and policy changes (action:copilot) and the cloud agent's website activity (actor:Copilot) with 180-day retention — it does not capture client-side prompts, so IDE-level telemetry needs its own answer. Proxy and firewall allowlists are documented per-plan, with a /meta API endpoint for the current domain set.

links.title: Reviewing audit logs for Copilot Business
Proxy and firewall settings for Copilot

items.title: VS Code device policies and the Copilot managed-settings plane
body: VS Code's ADMX/plist/policy.json set carries the agent lockdown: ChatAgentMode, ChatToolsAutoApprove, ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove, ChatAgentSandbox*, ChatAgentNetworkFilter with allowed/denied domains, ChatMCP / ChatAllowedMcpServers / ChatDeniedMcpServers / ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly, McpGalleryServiceUrl, ChatPlugins* and ChatStrictMarketplaces, ChatHooks / ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly, Claude3PIntegration / Codex3PIntegration, ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations and the CopilotOtel* export keys. Developer: Policy Diagnostics shows which source won.

The same keys arrive through GitHub's managed-settings.json (permissions deny/ask/allow, disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowedMcpServers, enabledPlugins, telemetry). Precedence in VS Code 1.128+: MDM-delivered managed settings, then server-managed, then the local file — and a Copilot managed setting outranks the equivalent VS Code policy.

links.title: VS Code AI settings for enterprises

riskNotes.note: Three of the four 2025–26 CVEs on this surface are prompt injection turned into code execution (settings-file rewrite in VS Code, shell metacharacters in the JetBrains plugin, consent-prompt bypass in the extension host). The vendor mitigations are approval prompts and the sandbox; the enterprise controls that survive a successful injection are ChatToolsAutoApprove=false, ChatAgentSandboxEnabled and the network filter.

The registry-based restriction matches on server name only and is bypassable by editing mcp.json; only the managed-settings allowlist (name, URL, stdio command) is a real boundary. Starting a server straight from mcp.json also skips the trust prompt.

Content exclusion is not honoured by edit and agent modes, and the IDE can still surface semantic information from excluded files. Local BYOK moves prompts off GitHub's ZDR contracts onto whatever the developer's provider retains.

Agent Host sessions can run Claude Agent SDK and Codex runtimes inside VS Code; unless Claude3PIntegration / Codex3PIntegration are set to false, a "Copilot" seat is also a third-party agent seat, with its own model and data path.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise licensing (seat assignment, enterprise teams synced from the IdP) plus the VS Code ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations device policy and Visual Studio ADMX

steps.title: Assign seats through enterprise teams or organisations
body: Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot > Manage: assign licences to users or enterprise teams; with Enterprise Managed Users, sync the team to an IdP group so access follows the IdP.

steps.title: Gate VS Code chat to approved GitHub organisations
body: Set the ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations policy to the list of organisation logins; chat, agents and inline suggestions stay off until the signed-in account belongs to one, which forces the organisation's policies to apply before any AI feature works.

steps.title: Block personal Copilot accounts in Visual Studio
body: Deploy the Visual Studio ADMX templates and use Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings to disable Copilot for individual accounts or Copilot Free.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow (Shell, Read, Edit, Domain selectors; GA 2026-09-09) for VS Code Agent Host sessions, plus PreToolUse hooks

steps.title: Pin deny / ask / allow rules in the managed file
body: Write permissions.deny, permissions.ask and permissions.allow with Shell(...), Read(...), Edit(...) and Domain(...) selectors. Deny wins from any source, ask forces a fresh approval that bypass mode cannot satisfy, and the effective allow list is the intersection of all sources.

steps.title: Confirm the client honours managed permissions
body: Managed permissions are enforced in VS Code sessions that use Agent Host, the Copilot app and the CLI; the reference matrix shows JetBrains honouring only permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, so JetBrains lockdown relies on that key and the sandbox.

steps.title: Add a PreToolUse hook as a second gate
body: VS Code runs .github/hooks/*.json and ~/.copilot/hooks; a PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision allow / deny / ask. Set ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly so only enterprise-managed hooks and policy-enabled plugins can register.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; the assessment inputs are the model-hosting page (providers, ZDR terms) and the Copilot Trust Center
controls.note: Treat GitHub plus each model provider (OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS/GCP/Anthropic, Google, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry/Fireworks) as the subprocessor set; the hosting page is the only first-party list and it changes with every model launch. The trust centre page did not render for automated fetch on 2026-09-10.

steps.title: Record the model-provider set and their retention terms
body: Use the hosting page to enumerate where each model runs and which retain data (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default; request the ZDR exemption).

controls.mechanism: Content exclusion (repository / organisation / enterprise) plus telemetry.captureContent=false with lockCaptureContent
controls.note: Content exclusion is a context filter, not DLP: it does not apply to edit and agent modes, symlinks or remote filesystems, and IDE-provided type information can still leak. Inline inspection of the prompt stream needs an SSE or endpoint DLP product.

steps.title: Exclude secret-bearing paths at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion (or Organization Settings > Copilot > Content exclusion): add fnmatch entries such as "*": ["**/.env"] and per-repository paths; changes propagate within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Keep prompt content out of the telemetry export
body: In managed-settings.json set telemetry.captureContent to false and telemetry.lockCaptureContent to true so users cannot turn content capture on.

controls.mechanism: VS Code policies ChatToolsAutoApprove, ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval, ChatAgentExtensionTools, BrowserChatTools, ChatAgentMode; Visual Studio "Disable Agent Mode"; managed permissions

steps.title: Remove global auto-approval and pick eligible tools
body: Set ChatToolsAutoApprove to false (it "disables manual approval completely for all tools in all workspaces") and use ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval to name the tools that may ever skip approval.

steps.title: Cut extension and browser tools
body: ChatAgentExtensionTools=false blocks tools contributed by third-party extensions; BrowserChatTools=false removes the integrated browser tool; ChatAgentMode=false removes agent mode entirely.

steps.title: Disable agent mode in Visual Studio where needed
body: Visual Studio 17.14.16+ honours Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings > Disable Agent Mode.

controls.mechanism: VS Code ChatAgentSandboxEnabled / AllowNetwork / AllowAutoApprove / AllowUnsandboxedCommands (macOS, Linux, WSL2; preview); JetBrains enterprise-managed sandbox (preview 2026-09-08); per-server MCP sandbox
controls.note: Visual Studio and the Xcode / Eclipse / Vim plugins have no sandbox. The VS Code setting chat.agent.sandbox.retryWithAllowNetworkRequests has no policy, so a sandboxed command can be retried with network unless allowNetwork is also false.

steps.title: Force the VS Code sandbox on and close its exits
body: Set ChatAgentSandboxEnabled=true, ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork=false and ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands=false; keep ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove false unless sandboxed commands may run unattended.

steps.title: Sandbox stdio MCP servers
body: In the server entry set sandboxEnabled: true with allowWrite paths and allowedDomains; sandboxed servers can only touch the paths and domains listed.

steps.title: Push the JetBrains sandbox policy from managed settings
body: The JetBrains plugin reads the managed sandbox policy (enablement, filesystem and network access, proxy, dev-tool and Keychain access) under GitHub Copilot > Sandbox — public preview.

controls.mechanism: The agent acts with the developer's own GitHub session; org OAuth-app access policy and PAT policies bound what the GitHub MCP server can reach
controls.note: There is no on-behalf-of exchange: tool calls carry the signed-in user's authority. The usable boundaries are the organisation's OAuth app access restrictions, fine-grained PAT approval and SSO enforcement on the GitHub MCP server, and the sandbox for local commands.

steps.title: Bound the GitHub MCP server with org access policies
body: Enforce the OAuth app access policy for third-party hosts, require approval of fine-grained PATs and keep SSO enforcement on so tokens must map to a recent SSO login.

controls.mechanism: CopilotSessionSync policy (VS Code) and the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy; Copilot Memory does not apply to IDEs
controls.note: IDE sessions have no persistent agent memory of their own; the exposure is session history synced to github.com and repository custom-instruction files, which the agent reads as trusted context.

steps.title: Decide whether IDE sessions sync to GitHub
body: Set the CopilotSessionSync policy (chat.sessionSync.enabled) to false to keep session history local; at the organisation level the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy controls the same sync for Copilot clients.

steps.title: Confirm Memory is out of scope for IDEs
body: The supported-surfaces table lists Copilot Memory as not supported in IDEs, the CLI and the app; the memory policy therefore governs github.com, the cloud agent and code review only.

controls.mechanism: VS Code two-step URL approval, Workspace Trust restricted mode, edit review flow; no configurable injection classifier
controls.note: Defences are structural (approvals, trust boundaries, sandbox), not detection. Prompt injection has produced RCE on this surface twice (CVE-2025-53773, CVE-2026-21516), so pair these with tool scoping and egress control rather than relying on them.

steps.title: Keep the structural defences on
body: Leave URL fetching on the two-step trust-domain-then-review flow, keep Workspace Trust so untrusted folders open in restricted mode with agents disabled, and require edit review before commits.

controls.mechanism: chat.tools.edits.autoApprove glob patterns, content exclusion for secret files, GitHub sign-in through the editor's account provider
controls.note: No vault integration: agents read whatever the developer's environment holds. The vendor lever is to keep secret files out of context and out of auto-approved edits.

steps.title: Require manual review for edits to secret files
body: Set chat.tools.edits.autoApprove with patterns such as "**/.env": false so those files always need explicit approval.

steps.title: Exclude secret files from context
body: Add **/.env and credential paths to organisation or enterprise content exclusion.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (name, URL wildcard, stdio command), ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly, McpGalleryServiceUrl registry, Visual Studio 2026 allowlist

steps.title: Publish the enterprise MCP allowlist
body: In .github-private/copilot/managed-settings.json set allowedMcpServers entries with serverName, serverUrl (wildcards allowed) or serverCommand arrays and deniedMcpServers for hard blocks; prerequisite is MCP servers in Copilot enabled and Restrict MCP access to registry servers set to Allow all.

steps.title: Make VS Code ignore user and workspace allowlists
body: Set ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly (managed key allowManagedMcpServersOnly) to true and ChatMCP to registry or none; point McpGalleryServiceUrl at a private registry if one exists.

steps.title: Treat the registry restriction as advisory
body: Registry-only enforcement matches on server name/ID and "can be bypassed by editing configuration files"; the cloud agent ignores it. Use it for discovery, not control.

controls.mechanism: permissions.ask rules and disableBypassPermissionsMode in managed settings; VS Code ChatToolsAutoApprove and ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove policies

steps.title: Kill bypass and Autopilot modes fleet-wide
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable"; VS Code and the app then reject auto-approve settings, the CLI drops --yolo / --allow-all, and JetBrains blocks Bypass Approvals and Autopilot.

steps.title: Force approval on the operations that matter
body: Put Shell(git push*), Edit(**/.env) and similar selectors under permissions.ask; ask entries require a fresh approval every time and cannot be satisfied by saved approvals.

steps.title: Disable terminal auto-approval rules
body: ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove=false removes the regex-based terminal auto-approval, whose parser has documented gaps around aliases and complex syntax.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise-level custom agents (AI Controls, REST API), enterprise plugin standards (enabledPlugins, strictKnownMarketplaces), private MCP registry
controls.note: The enterprise can publish approved agents, plugins and MCP servers, but there is no inventory of what developers actually run and no reconciliation; ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization is the nearest thing to "deny what is not registered".

steps.title: Publish approved agents and plugins centrally
body: Define enterprise custom agents under AI Controls or the REST API, and in managed settings set enabledPlugins (plugin@marketplace) with strictKnownMarketplaces so only listed marketplaces are trusted.

steps.title: Block unregistered customisation in VS Code
body: ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization blocks standalone user and workspace skills, agents, hooks, instructions and MCP servers, leaving only policy-supplied plugins.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise/organisation audit log (action:copilot, 180 days, streamable) for policy and licensing events; CopilotOtel* / telemetry.* managed OpenTelemetry export for session content
controls.note: The audit log "does not capture client session data, such as the prompts a user sends"; session-level evidence exists only if the enterprise runs an OTLP collector and pins the export in managed settings.

steps.title: Pin the OpenTelemetry export in managed settings
body: Set telemetry.enabled, telemetry.endpoint, telemetry.protocol, telemetry.headers and telemetry.serviceName; when managed, users cannot override the exporter and CopilotOtelOutfile prevents local file export.

steps.title: Stream the audit log
body: Search action:copilot for licence and policy changes; stream the enterprise audit log to a SIEM for retention beyond 180 days.

controls.mechanism: No discovery feature; VS Code AllowedExtensions and ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations prevent rather than find
controls.note: Use the AllowedExtensions policy to stop unsanctioned AI extensions installing and the approved-organisations gate to stop personal Copilot accounts; discovery of what is already running belongs to endpoint or SSE tooling.

steps.title: Restrict installable extensions
body: Set AllowedExtensions (extensions.allowed) to the sanctioned publisher and extension list.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise policy "Disabled everywhere" per feature, seat removal, ChatAgentMode=false, Visual Studio ADMX Disable Copilot

steps.title: Disable at enterprise scope, not organisation scope
body: Within one enterprise the least restrictive organisation policy usually wins for a user, so set the feature policy to Disabled everywhere on the enterprise AI controls tab to make it stick.

steps.title: Remove agent mode on the device
body: ChatAgentMode=false disables agent mode and side-effect tools in VS Code regardless of account; the Visual Studio ADMX policy disables Copilot outright.

controls.mechanism: None from the vendor; the OS sandbox and PreToolUse hooks are the only device-side hooks
controls.note: Endpoint agents that instrument coding agents by name are the answer; the vendor exposes PreToolUse hooks and an OTLP export an EDR integration can consume.

controls.mechanism: Organisation and enterprise custom instructions and custom agents, ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization, ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly
controls.note: Repository .github instruction files are read as trusted context and are writable by anyone with push access — CVE-2025-53773 exploited exactly that pattern against settings files. The enterprise can force its own instructions but cannot version-pin repository ones.

steps.title: Apply organisation instructions and managed agents
body: Enable github.copilot.chat.organizationInstructions.enabled and showOrganizationAndEnterpriseAgents so organisation-level instructions and custom agents are applied and offered by default.

steps.title: Block user and workspace overrides
body: ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization removes standalone user and workspace instructions, agents, skills and hooks; ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly keeps hooks to managed sources.

controls.mechanism: No manifests or signatures for extensions, plugins or MCP servers
controls.note: Plugins install from marketplaces by name; strictKnownMarketplaces limits sources but nothing verifies content. Record extension and plugin versions yourself.

controls.mechanism: VS Code ChatAgentNetworkFilter with ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains / DeniedNetworkDomains, sandbox allowNetwork, Domain() managed permissions, documented proxy allowlist

steps.title: Turn on the agent network filter with an allowlist
body: Set ChatAgentNetworkFilter=true; with both domain lists empty all domains are blocked, so add ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains entries (wildcards allowed) and let ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains take precedence.

steps.title: Deny domains in managed permissions
body: Use Domain(...) selectors under permissions.deny for hosts the agent's fetch and browser tools must never reach; host matching is case-insensitive and *.example.com covers subdomains.

steps.title: Allowlist the Copilot service domains at the proxy
body: Permit *.githubcopilot.com plus the plan-specific *.business or *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com, the github.com login and copilot_internal endpoints and copilot-proxy.githubusercontent.com; pull the current set from gh api meta.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable to vendor-hosted models; local BYOK models (Ollama etc.) are the organisation's own artefacts
controls.note: Disable local BYOK through the "Configure custom models" policy if unscanned local models are a concern.

advisories.title: CVE-2025-53773 — GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio command injection via prompt injection (settings rewrite to enable YOLO mode); GitHub advisory GHSA-3m2x-p87c-pwv6
CVE-2026-21516 — GitHub Copilot for JetBrains RCE (command injection, plugin < 1.5.63); Microsoft CNA record — MSRC page not machine-readable, no GitHub advisory

RoguePilot — hidden HTML-comment instructions in an issue drive Copilot in a Codespace to leak GITHUB_TOKEN (Orca Security research; no CVE, no first-party advisory)
