tools.name: GitHub Copilot SDK

variants.name: Copilot SDK (Node.js, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, Java; GA 2026-06-02)
Headless Copilot CLI server (copilot --headless) for backend services and multi-tenant deployments
Cloud sessions (work runs on GitHub-hosted compute, published to github.com/copilot/tasks)

summary: The Copilot SDK embeds the agent runtime behind Copilot CLI in a customer-hosted application: the SDK talks JSON-RPC to a Copilot CLI process (bundled, local, or a persistent --headless server) that plans, calls tools, edits files and streams turns. The customer owns request routing, user authentication, session ownership, tool registration, secrets and scaling; GitHub supplies the model access and the permission model the CLI already enforces.

Inference goes to the Copilot API using a GitHub OAuth token, a fine-grained PAT, a server-to-server installation token, or — under BYOK — straight to OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, bypassing GitHub entirely. Session state lives on the host under COPILOT_HOME/session-state/{sessionId} (or an application-provided sessionFs); cloud sessions run on GitHub compute and appear in the agents panel.

The controls are code: onPermissionRequest (deny-by-default), onPreToolUse allow / deny / ask / modify, mode "empty" with an explicit availableTools list, per-session gitHubToken, sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds, and an OpenTelemetry TelemetryConfig with W3C trace propagation. Enterprise managed permissions are advertised for the SDK at GA; the managed-settings reference does not list the SDK as a client, so treat that as unverified.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Any Copilot subscriber including Free; non-Copilot users via BYOK. Sessions bill AI credits to the token's owner; usage is exposed as assistant.usage and session.usage.getMetrics (nano-AI units).

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API with the session's GitHub token, or BYOK ProviderConfig (type openai / azure / anthropic, baseUrl, apiKey, wireApi) with prompts sent directly to the provider; Azure managed identity can supply bearer tokens instead of keys.

facts.label: Data leaving the host
facts.value: Prompts, tool results and file context to the Copilot API or the BYOK provider; OTLP traces only where configured; cloud sessions publish to github.com/copilot/tasks/{sessionId}; the CLI's telemetry stays on unless COPILOT_OFFLINE=true.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Session state persists on the host filesystem (or a shared volume) with a 30-minute idle timeout in headless mode; GitHub-hosted models follow the Copilot ZDR terms (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default); BYOK providers apply their own retention.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot SDK how-tos: setup, authentication, features, hooks, integrations, observability, troubleshooting.

items.title: Multi-user server mode — the isolation checklist
body: Set gitHubToken per session so content exclusion, model routing and quota follow the requesting user; use mode: "empty" and an explicit availableTools list (custom:*, mcp:tool) so ambient OS tools are off; encode tenant and user in session IDs and check ownership before resume or delete; set sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds; use baseDirectory and sessionFs to isolate runtime state. The docs list the pitfalls plainly: default mode copilot-cli exposes the host filesystem, one shared GitHub token loses per-user authorisation, client-provided session IDs cannot be trusted.

Deployment patterns: an isolated CLI per user (strongest; SOC 2 / HIPAA), a shared CLI with per-session isolation, or shared collaborative sessions that need application locking. There is no built-in auth between SDK and CLI — bind --headless to loopback or a private network.

items.title: Hooks as the policy layer
body: onPermissionRequest is deny-by-default: file writes, shell commands and URL fetches fail unless the application approves. onPreToolUse returns permissionDecision allow / deny / ask with modifiedArgs, additionalContext and suppressOutput; onPostToolUse can redact secrets and audit; onUserPromptSubmitted / onUserPromptTransformed filter or replace prompts; onSessionStart / End and onErrorOccurred carry sessionId for correlation. All run inline in the turn.

riskNotes.note: The documented anti-pattern is one service token for every user; with it, content exclusion and quotas collapse to the service account's view. Per-session gitHubToken and backend ownership checks on session IDs are the vendor's answer.
The SDK–CLI JSON-RPC link has no authentication; a headless CLI bound to 0.0.0.0 is an open agent runtime with whatever token it was started with.
No built-in rate limiting or session cap: the SDK exposes quota and usage events but the application must enforce limits and evict idle sessions.
MCP servers and custom tools are registered by the application; nothing verifies them, and the default tool mode inherits the CLI's host tools.

controls.mechanism: Per-session runtime state under COPILOT_HOME/session-state/{sessionId}, sessionFs to route state into application storage, sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds, application-enforced ownership checks

steps.title: Isolate and expire session state
body: Encode tenant and user in session IDs, verify ownership before resume or delete, set sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds (15–30 minutes for chat) and use baseDirectory / sessionFs to keep state per process or in your own store.

controls.mechanism: No evaluation harness in the SDK; GitHub evaluates hosted models vendor-side
controls.note: Build evals in your own CI against the SDK; the application card describes GitHub's internal benchmarks and red teaming only.

controls.mechanism: TelemetryConfig (OTLP endpoint, protocol, exporter type, capture content, source name) on the client; W3C traceparent / tracestate propagation between SDK, CLI and tool handlers; usage events

steps.title: Configure OTLP export and trace propagation
body: Create the client with telemetry: { otlpEndpoint, otlpProtocol, exporterType, captureContent } — Python, Go and .NET inject trace context automatically, Node.js needs onGetTraceContext; tool handlers receive traceparent for child spans.

steps.title: Capture usage per turn
body: Subscribe to assistant.usage and session.usage_info events and call session.usage.getMetrics for per-model totals.

controls.mechanism: GitHub OAuth per user with gitHubToken set per session; service-to-server installation tokens for services; application-level authentication and session ownership

steps.title: Authenticate users, not the runtime
body: Pass each requesting user's GitHub token on the session (gitHubToken) so quota, content exclusion and model policy resolve to that user; reserve service tokens for internal tools.

steps.title: Choose the auth path per deployment
body: GitHub OAuth for user-facing apps, short-lived installation access tokens for server-to-server, BYOK where GitHub auth is not wanted.

controls.mechanism: Server-to-server installation access tokens (short-lived) and GITHUB_COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID stamping requests with the product identity
controls.note: The agent's identity is the token's identity; there is no agent-specific credential or registry. Rotate installation tokens and stamp the integration ID for attribution.

steps.title: Stamp the integration identity
body: Set GITHUB_COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID on the runtime so requests are attributed and routed by product.

controls.mechanism: Provider keys via ProviderConfig.apiKey or Azure managed-identity bearer callbacks; platform secret managers recommended; no vault integration in the SDK

steps.title: Prefer managed identity over static keys
body: Use the Azure managed identity setup so the SDK obtains bearer tokens through callbacks instead of storing apiKey values.

steps.title: Keep keys in a secret manager
body: The scaling guide's production checklist names Vault or Kubernetes Secrets for credentials and persistent volumes for session state.

controls.mechanism: onPermissionRequest (deny-by-default) and onPreToolUse returning permissionDecision allow / deny / ask with modifiedArgs; enterprise managed permissions announced for SDK sessions

steps.title: Implement the permission handler
body: Without an onPermissionRequest handler every file write, shell command and URL fetch is denied; implement it as a policy decision, not approve_all.

steps.title: Gate every tool call in onPreToolUse
body: Return { permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason } for disallowed tools or arguments, constrain modifiedArgs (timeouts, allowed directories) and always return an explicit decision.

steps.title: Check whether managed permissions reach your sessions
body: The GA post lists enterprise-managed permissions for agent operations as an SDK enterprise feature; the managed-settings client matrix does not name the SDK — verify with a deny rule before relying on it.

controls.mechanism: mode "empty" plus an explicit availableTools allowlist (custom:*, mcp:name, builtin:*); MCP servers chosen per session

steps.title: Start from no tools
body: Set mode: "empty" so CLI defaults and ambient OS tools are disabled, then list availableTools explicitly; avoid builtin:* without review.

controls.mechanism: Per-session gitHubToken versus a single runtime service token; BYOK keys per session; loopback-only headless binding

steps.title: Scope GitHub auth to the requesting user
body: Set gitHubToken per session; the docs warn that sharing one token across users breaks content exclusion and quota attribution.

steps.title: Protect the SDK–CLI link
body: There is no built-in auth between SDK and CLI; keep copilot --headless on loopback or inside a private network.

controls.mechanism: sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds, 30-minute idle cleanup, recommended concurrent-session cap and eviction, account.getQuota; no built-in rate limiting
controls.note: Quota is visible, not enforced: the application must cap sessions and spend. The CLI's --max-ai-credits applies to programmatic CLI runs, not documented for SDK sessions.

steps.title: Cap and evict sessions
body: Limit concurrent active sessions (the guide suggests 50), evict the oldest idle ones, set sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds and delete expired sessions.

steps.title: Watch quota
body: Poll account.getQuota for remaining entitlement and reset dates, and meter assistant.usage per turn.

controls.mechanism: onUserPromptSubmitted / onUserPromptTransformed hooks to filter or rewrite prompts and onPreToolUse to gate resulting tool calls; no built-in classifier

steps.title: Screen prompts and tool outputs in hooks
body: Filter or annotate prompts in onUserPromptSubmitted, inspect model-facing content in onUserPromptTransformed, and deny suspicious tool calls in onPreToolUse.

controls.mechanism: onPostToolUse redaction, captureContent=false in telemetry, per-user token so content exclusion applies; no inspection of the prompt stream by the vendor

steps.title: Redact in onPostToolUse and keep content out of traces
body: Use onPostToolUse to redact secrets from tool results before they reach the model; leave TelemetryConfig captureContent off in production.

controls.mechanism: onPermissionRequest approvals and onPreToolUse "ask" decisions routed to the application's own approval UI

steps.title: Route privileged actions to a human
body: Return permissionDecision "ask" (interactive) or hold the onPermissionRequest promise until an operator approves for shell, write and network operations.

controls.mechanism: Per-session gitHubToken makes GitHub retrieval and content exclusion run as the requesting user; other data sources are the application's tools

steps.title: Never retrieve as a shared principal
body: Set gitHubToken per session; for custom tools, pass the user's identity into the tool handler rather than a service credential.

controls.mechanism: Inherits Copilot CLI's local sandbox (MXC) and permission model; isolated CLI per user; cloud sessions on GitHub compute
controls.note: The SDK docs do not describe enabling the local sandbox from the SDK; the CLI's sandbox.* managed settings and OS isolation of the host process are the containment.

steps.title: Isolate the runtime per tenant
body: Run one CLI server per user on its own port for compliance-grade isolation; a shared CLI gives only session-level separation.

steps.title: Offload risky work to cloud sessions
body: Create sessions with the cloud option so execution happens on GitHub-hosted compute and is visible at github.com/copilot/tasks/{sessionId}; requires cloud-agent entitlement and organisation policies permitting remote control.

controls.mechanism: No registry; tools, MCP servers and agents are whatever the application registers per session
controls.note: Keep the availableTools list and MCP configuration in version control and stamp GITHUB_COPILOT_INTEGRATION_ID so GitHub can attribute the integration.

controls.mechanism: Hooks for audit logging (onPreToolUse / onPostToolUse with sessionId), OTLP traces, cloud sessions visible on github.com; no GitHub audit-log events for local SDK sessions

steps.title: Log decisions from hooks
body: Record every permissionDecision and tool result in onPreToolUse / onPostToolUse, keyed by the invocation's sessionId, alongside the OTLP export.

controls.mechanism: deleteSession and session eviction, revoking the session's GitHub token or installation, stopping the headless CLI; no enterprise policy names the SDK
controls.note: The Copilot CLI policy gates the underlying runtime for enterprise seats; the SDK docs do not name a policy of their own.

steps.title: Terminate sessions and drain servers
body: Call deleteSession for the affected sessions, drain active sessions before stopping the CLI server, and revoke the token or app installation the runtime uses.

controls.mechanism: OTLP traces and hook logs feed a SIEM; no vendor detections for SDK sessions
Session state is plain files on the host or a networked filesystem; encryption and key custody are the deployer's
controls.note: Mount encrypted persistent volumes for ~/.copilot/session-state or route state through sessionFs into an encrypted store.

controls.mechanism: No retrieval store in the SDK; any corpus is the application's own tool or MCP server
MCP servers run as separate processes and are selected per session; availableTools mcp:* patterns; no verification or pinning

steps.title: Choose MCP servers per session and name their tools
body: Register only trusted servers per session and allowlist their tools with mcp:tool patterns; the application card places responsibility for server trustworthiness on the developer.

controls.mechanism: No manifests or signatures for tools, MCP servers or the bundled CLI
controls.note: Pin the SDK and CLI versions in your dependency manifest; the bundled-CLI path updates the runtime with the SDK package.

controls.mechanism: BYOK baseUrl pins the model endpoint; headless CLI bound to loopback; network egress is the host's responsibility

steps.title: Bind the runtime privately
body: Run copilot --headless on loopback (default) or a private host; expose it through your application, never directly.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable to hosted models; BYOK local models (Ollama, OpenAI-compatible) are the deployer's artefacts

tools.name: Gemini CLI

variants.name: Gemini CLI (npm @google/gemini-cli, v0.59.0 stable 2026-09-08)

summary: Google's open-source terminal coding agent (Apache-2.0, npm @google/gemini-cli): a ReAct loop over built-in file, shell, web-fetch and search tools, MCP servers, hooks, extensions, sub-agents and skills, driven by a present developer. Inference is remote — Gemini via the Code Assist service (Google Workspace account with a Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence and a Google Cloud project), a Gemini API key, or Vertex AI; the developer runs the harness on their own machine.

Prompts, file contents and tool output leave the device for the chosen Google endpoint; session transcripts, checkpoints and the shadow-git history stay under ~/.gemini. Usage statistics go to Google unless privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled is false; OpenTelemetry export is off unless telemetry.enabled is set, and logPrompts decides whether prompt text rides along.

Two admin planes. Locally, a root-owned system settings.json (/etc/gemini-cli, C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli, /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli) takes final precedence over user and workspace settings and carries tools.core, mcp.allowed, tools.sandbox, security.auth.enforcedType, security.disableYoloMode and telemetry.*; admin-tier policy TOML files under the same directory outrank every other policy tier. Remotely, the Enterprise Admin Controls page describes a Management Console (strict mode, extensions, MCP on/off, an MCP allowlist that strips local command/args/env, required MCP servers, unmanaged capabilities) that the client enforces and users cannot override — the console itself is reached through a go-link that resolves only to geminicli.com, so its location and licence gating could not be verified.

The consumer path is closing: the vendor's authentication page states that Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18 for unpaid-tier and Google One users, and the Code Assist for individuals notice says Login with Google no longer serves the CLI for individual, Google AI Pro and Ultra tiers. Organisations stay on Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, an API key or Vertex AI.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Gemini Code Assist Standard (1,500 requests/user/day) and Enterprise (2,000) include the CLI, with quota shared with Code Assist agent mode; Gemini API key (unpaid 250/day Flash-only, or paid) and Vertex AI (express or pay-as-you-go) are the other paths. The quota page still lists the free Google-account tier, but the authentication page says that tier moved to Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Remote only: Code Assist API for licensed Workspace/Cloud accounts (needs GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and the Gemini for Cloud API), Gemini API with GEMINI_API_KEY, or Vertex AI with ADC / service-account JSON / GOOGLE_API_KEY. GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL and GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL redirect the API calls through an organisation proxy.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, context files, tool output and file contents to the model endpoint; anonymous usage statistics to Google (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled, default true); OTLP telemetry to a local collector or Google Cloud Logging/Trace/Monitoring only when telemetry.enabled is set, with telemetry.logPrompts governing prompt text.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Code Assist Standard/Enterprise: stateless service, prompts and responses are not stored in Google Cloud unless the admin turns on logging to a Cloud Logging bucket; "Google doesn't use your data to train our models without your permission". API-key and Vertex paths fall under the Gemini API (unpaid/paid) and Google Cloud terms respectively.

facts.label: Enterprise admin planes
facts.value: System settings.json and admin policy TOML on the machine (GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH overrides the path); Management Console controls (strict mode, extensions, MCP allowlist and required servers, unmanaged capabilities) enforced by the client and non-overridable locally.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: geminicli.com/docs — Enterprise configuration, Settings reference, Policy engine, Sandboxing, Trusted folders, Hooks, MCP servers, Extensions, Telemetry, Terms & privacy.

items.title: Settings precedence and the system override file
body: Settings merge in the order system defaults (system-defaults.json), user (~/.gemini/settings.json), workspace (.gemini/settings.json), then the system override (settings.json in /etc/gemini-cli, C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli or /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli), which wins; arrays such as includeDirectories and objects such as mcpServers are merged rather than replaced. Environment variables and command-line flags sit above the files. GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH and GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_PATH relocate the system files, so pin them or the directory ACLs with MDM.

items.title: Policy engine tiers
body: Tool calls are decided by TOML rules (toolName, mcpName, argsPattern, commandPrefix / commandRegex, decision allow / deny / ask_user, priority 0-999, modes, interactive). Tiers are default 1, extension 2, workspace 3 (currently disabled), user 4, admin 5; admin rules in the system policies directory always outrank user rules, and a global deny removes the tool from the model's context. ask_user is treated as deny in headless runs. Out of the box, read-only tools are allowed and write tools and run_shell_command ask; yolo mode adds a high-priority allow-all rule.

items.title: Management Console controls
body: The Enterprise Admin Controls page lists Strict Mode (blocks yolo mode), an Extensions toggle, an MCP toggle, an MCP allowlist (locally configured servers not in the list are ignored, and the client clears command, args, env and cwd so only remote servers survive), Required MCP Servers (injected, overriding same-named local entries, with authProviderType / targetServiceAccount / oauth fields) and Unmanaged Capabilities (currently Agent Skills). All are described as enforced globally and immutable locally. The page's console link (goo.gle/manage-gemini-cli) redirected to the geminicli.com home page on 2026-09-10, so treat the delivery path as unverified.

riskNotes.note: GEMINI.md context files are loaded from the repository, its parents and any directory a tool touches; the first public exploit (Tracebit, 2025-07) hid instructions in a GEMINI.md and chained a payload behind an allowlisted grep. Trusted folders keep workspace settings, .env, MCP servers, hooks and context files off until the user trusts the folder; nothing classifies the content.

--yolo and per-session "always allow" remain user choices unless the admin sets security.disableYoloMode / security.disableAlwaysAllow or Strict Mode; GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g (CVSS 10.0) showed yolo mode ignoring the tool allowlist and headless runs trusting the workspace automatically.

Extensions install from any GitHub URL or local path and bundle MCP servers, hooks, commands, sub-agents and skills; only the admin extensions toggle and the MCP allowlist bound the source, and neither pins content.

API keys live in plaintext in .gemini/.env or shell profiles; telemetry.logPrompts defaults are stated inconsistently across the vendor's own pages (true on the telemetry page, false on the settings reference), so set it explicitly in the system file.

controls.mechanism: Google account sign-in gated by a Gemini Code Assist licence and Google Cloud project IAM; security.auth.enforcedType in the system settings file

steps.title: Force the organisation's auth path
body: In the system settings.json set security.auth.enforcedType (the enterprise page's example is "oauth-personal") so a mismatched cached credential triggers re-authentication rather than silently using an API key.

steps.title: Licence and project
body: Company, school and Workspace accounts need a Gemini Code Assist licence, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set, the Gemini for Cloud API enabled and IAM access on that project; without them Sign in with Google does not serve the CLI.

controls.mechanism: Admin-tier policy engine TOML plus BeforeTool hooks in the system settings file

steps.title: Ship admin policies
body: Place [[rule]] files in /etc/gemini-cli/policies (or the macOS / Windows equivalents): admin tier 5 outranks user and workspace tiers; use commandPrefix / commandRegex for shell, mcpName for servers, decision deny with denyMessage.

steps.title: Add a BeforeTool gate
body: A hooks.BeforeTool command in the system settings receives tool_name and tool_input and blocks with {"decision": "deny"} or exit code 2; keep it there rather than in user settings, which users edit.

controls.mechanism: Google Cloud terms and the Code Assist security, privacy and compliance page consumed by the organisation's TPRM platform
controls.note: The CLI is covered by the Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise commitments (stateless service, no training without permission, VPC Service Controls) when used with that licence; the API-key and Vertex paths carry different terms, listed on the CLI's Terms and Privacy page.

steps.title: Record which terms apply
body: Match the auth path the organisation enforces to its terms row on the Terms and Privacy page and file the Code Assist compliance page as the vendor evidence.

controls.mechanism: BeforeModel / AfterModel hooks for redaction; no vendor DLP
controls.note: Hooks can rewrite the outbound request and filter the response, and inherited environment variables matching TOKEN / SECRET / PASSWORD / KEY patterns are redacted before MCP servers see them; content inspection of prompts and uploads is the organisation's own hook or a proxy at GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL.

steps.title: Wire a redaction hook
body: Configure hooks.BeforeModel and hooks.AfterModel commands in the system settings file to inspect and redact the request and response payloads.

controls.mechanism: tools.core allowlist, tools.confirmationRequired, per-server includeTools / excludeTools, mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded in the system settings file

steps.title: Allowlist built-in tools
body: Set tools.core in the system settings (for example ReadFileTool, GlobTool, ShellTool(ls)); tools.exclude is deprecated in favour of the allowlist.

steps.title: Scope MCP tools
body: Define mcpServers centrally and set mcp.allowed to the same names, or users can add their own; trim each server with includeTools / excludeTools and keep trust unset so calls still confirm.

steps.title: Keep confirmation on specific tools
body: tools.confirmationRequired forces approval for named tools even when tools.allowed would skip it.

controls.mechanism: tools.sandbox (docker / podman / sandbox-exec), Seatbelt profiles, tools.sandboxNetworkAccess

steps.title: Enforce a container sandbox
body: Set tools.sandbox to "docker" or "podman" in the system settings so tool execution runs in ghcr.io/google/gemini-cli (or a custom image via tools.sandbox.image) with the workspace mounted at the same path.

steps.title: Pick a macOS profile
body: On macOS the default Seatbelt profile is permissive-open; choose restrictive-* or strict-* and a *-proxied variant via SEATBELT_PROFILE when network must go through a proxy.

controls.mechanism: Per-user cached OAuth credential; Vertex AI service accounts; MCP OAuth per server; GEMINI_CLI_HOME for job isolation
controls.note: The agent runs with the developer's Google identity and whatever shell credentials it inherits; required MCP servers can carry targetServiceAccount / authProviderType, and shared runners can point GEMINI_CLI_HOME at a per-job directory, but there is no on-behalf-of exchange for the agent itself.

steps.title: Isolate shared runners
body: Set GEMINI_CLI_HOME per job so credentials, trust decisions and history do not leak between users on a shared machine.

controls.mechanism: Trusted folders gate context and .env loading; auto memory is experimental, off by default and approval-gated; checkpointing snapshots before edits
controls.note: The settings reference lists security.folderTrust.enabled as default true while the Trusted Folders page says the feature is disabled by default; set it explicitly. The global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md is user-writable and no admin lock is documented.

steps.title: Require folder trust
body: Set security.folderTrust.enabled to true in the system settings; untrusted folders then skip workspace settings, .env, MCP servers, extensions, custom commands and automatic context loading. Do not ship GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true or --skip-trust outside CI.

steps.title: Keep auto memory off
body: Leave experimental.autoMemory false; when enabled it mines ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats and proposes memory and skill updates that still need user approval.

controls.mechanism: Not offered; structural mitigations only
controls.note: No injection or jailbreak classifier is documented. The defences are trusted folders, ask_user policies on write tools, the post-2025-07 shell-command validation fix and hooks the organisation writes; treat every GEMINI.md, MCP response and fetched page as untrusted.

controls.mechanism: ${VAR} substitution in settings for MCP headers and env; automatic redaction of secret-named inherited variables
controls.note: API keys are read from GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY, shell profiles or a plaintext .gemini/.env; nothing vaults them, and variables set in .gemini/.env bypass the automatic exclusions. Prefer Sign in with Google (cached OAuth) or Vertex ADC over long-lived keys.

steps.title: Reference secrets, do not inline them
body: Use "$VAR_NAME" / "${VAR_NAME}" substitution in mcpServers env and headers so the system settings file carries no literal tokens.

controls.mechanism: mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded, the Management Console MCP allowlist and required servers, the extensions toggle
controls.note: Allowlists are by server name and URL; no content-hash pinning or tool-definition scanning is documented. v0.59.0 fixed SSRF in MCP OAuth metadata discovery.

steps.title: Allowlist servers centrally
body: Define mcpServers and mcp.allowed in the system settings; the enterprise page warns that mcpServers without mcp.allowed still lets users add their own.

steps.title: Use the console allowlist where available
body: The Management Console MCP allowlist ignores unlisted local servers and clears command / args / env / cwd, so only the listed remote servers connect; Required MCP Servers inject corporate servers with their own auth.

steps.title: Bound extensions
body: Extensions bundle MCP servers, hooks, commands and skills from any GitHub URL; disable extension installation with the console Extensions control, or review each with gemini extensions list.

controls.mechanism: ask_user default policy on write tools; security.disableYoloMode, security.disableAlwaysAllow; Strict Mode in the console

steps.title: Remove the bypasses
body: Set security.disableYoloMode true (blocks --yolo even when flagged) and security.disableAlwaysAllow true (removes "Always allow" from confirmations) in the system settings; leave security.enablePermanentToolApproval false.

steps.title: Strict Mode
body: Where the Management Console is in use, Strict Mode prevents yolo mode globally and cannot be overridden locally.

controls.mechanism: Central mcpServers plus mcp.allowed in the system settings; Management Console MCP allowlist and required servers
controls.note: The admin allowlist is the only approved-server record and covers MCP servers only; extensions, sub-agents and skills have no registry beyond the on/off toggles.

steps.title: Treat the allowlist as the record
body: Keep the mcpServers / mcp.allowed block (or the console allowlist) under change control as the authoritative list of approved tool servers.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry export to Google Cloud Logging / Trace / Monitoring via telemetry.target gcp; Code Assist admin logging to a Cloud Logging bucket
controls.note: Telemetry is emitted by the client, so it is only as tamper-resistant as the system settings that turn it on; the Gemini for Google Cloud audit-logging page does not say whether CLI requests appear in Cloud Audit Logs, and Data Access logs must be enabled.

steps.title: Export telemetry centrally
body: In the system settings set telemetry.enabled true, telemetry.target "gcp" and decide telemetry.logPrompts explicitly (the enterprise page recommends false); a "Gemini CLI Monitoring" dashboard template exists in Cloud Monitoring.

steps.title: Turn on Code Assist logging
body: The Gemini Code Assist administrator settings carry a Logging setting (default disabled) that stores user input and responses in a Cloud Logging bucket for Standard/Enterprise.

controls.mechanism: Not offered
controls.note: Discover installs with software inventory or EDR: the npm package @google/gemini-cli, the gemini binary, ~/.gemini and the Docker image ghcr.io/google/gemini-cli. An enforced auth type makes personal API-key use a detectable settings mismatch.

controls.mechanism: Licence and IAM revocation on the Google Cloud project; console MCP / extensions toggles; system settings tools.core
controls.note: Removing the Code Assist licence or project IAM stops Sign in with Google sessions, but a developer with a Gemini API key keeps working unless security.auth.enforcedType and network egress rules deny that path.

steps.title: Cut the licensed path
body: Revoke the user's Gemini Code Assist licence or the IAM binding on the Google Cloud project the CLI authenticates against.

controls.mechanism: EDR around the process; BeforeTool hooks as the pre-tool-call integration point
controls.note: Hooks in the system settings can call an endpoint agent before every tool call and deny on its verdict; otherwise watch for the sandbox container, writes under ~/.gemini and child processes of the gemini binary.

controls.mechanism: GEMINI.md hierarchy with context.fileName; GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD full replacement; trusted folders gate project context
controls.note: GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD replaces the entire built-in prompt from any file and has no documented admin lock; project GEMINI.md files load from the workspace and any directory a tool touches, subject only to folder trust.

steps.title: Fix the context file names
body: Set context.fileName in the system settings to the reviewed file names the organisation uses and require folder trust so untrusted clones do not inject context.

controls.mechanism: Not verified
controls.note: Releases are published on GitHub and npm; whether the npm package carries provenance attestations or a signed SBOM was not checked on 2026-09-10. Nothing manifests the extensions and MCP servers a session loads.

controls.mechanism: GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL / GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL proxy overrides; tools.sandboxNetworkAccess; *-proxied Seatbelt profiles; MCP env HTTP_PROXY
controls.note: Model traffic can be pointed at an organisation gateway and sandboxed tools can be denied network or forced through a proxy, but web-fetch, MCP servers outside the sandbox and the CLI process itself are bounded only by the host network policy; Code Assist supports VPC Service Controls on the service side.

steps.title: Route the model calls
body: Set GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL or GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL to the organisation's AI gateway and deny direct egress to the Google endpoints.

steps.title: Deny sandbox network
body: Keep tools.sandboxNetworkAccess false, or use a proxied Seatbelt profile so tool traffic exits through the proxy only.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable
controls.note: No model artifacts are loaded locally; every auth path is a remote Google endpoint.

advisories.title: GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g: RCE via workspace trust and tool allowlisting bypasses (CVSS 10.0); @google/gemini-cli < 0.39.1 and 0.40.0-preview.2, run-gemini-cli < 0.1.22
Tracebit: GEMINI.md prompt injection plus shell allowlist bypass for silent exfiltration; fixed v0.1.14 (2025-07-25)

tools.name: Hermes Agent
summary: An open-source (MIT) personal agent runtime — a competing product to OpenClaw, not a variant of it, with a one-command migration from it. Its posture centres on per-command approval with dangerous-command detection, DM pairing, fully isolated per-profile state, and sandboxed execution across multiple terminal backends.

items.title: Approval-first execution and isolated state
body: Execution goes through command approval with dangerous-command detection — blocked actions return a tool error naming the denied command rather than silently proceeding — and the first DM claims exclusive access to a deployment. Profiles are fully isolated (own memory store, session database and skills directory), subagents run isolated, and sandboxed execution spans local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona and Vercel Sandbox backends with container hardening and namespace isolation.

The governance trade-off to weigh: Hermes is a self-improving agent that writes its own skills from experience, which is also the feature demanding the most trust — an organisation sanctioning it should decide whether self-modification is acceptable and pin the approval policy accordingly.

links.title: Hermes Agent FAQ (approvals, pairing, profile isolation)

tools.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (web, desktop and Work)

variants.name: ChatGPT desktop app (macOS, Windows MSIX, Linux preview)
ChatGPT web (chatgpt.com)
ChatGPT Work (Work Local and Work Cloud)
Built-in browser (browser_use) and Chrome extension

summary: The current desktop app bundles Chat, Work and Codex, and is governed by the same managed-configuration system as Codex — requirements.toml cloud policies and the com.openai.codex MDM domain — plus workspace admin controls for plugins, apps, memory and identity from the ChatGPT admin panel.

Inference is at OpenAI for every mode. Chat and Work Cloud run entirely on OpenAI infrastructure (Work Cloud in VM-backed sandboxes with a hosted browser whose cookies stay separate from the device); Work Local runs on the desktop app with the Codex sandbox, computer use and the built-in browser, and the vendor states that relevant file excerpts, prompts, screenshots and browser content may be sent to OpenAI to complete a task.

Enterprise administration is role-based (Owner, Admin, Member, Analytics Viewer plus custom roles, with an explicit Off in any role denying), provisioned by SCIM, with plugins off by default on Enterprise and Edu, per-connection action controls, a GPT actions domain allowlist, access-token lifetime limits, service accounts, and a Compliance API whose records live 30 days at source.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Business, Enterprise and Edu carry the admin controls; plugins default on for Business and off for Enterprise and Edu.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Work Cloud runs the Codex harness in an isolated OpenAI environment; the web cannot access local files, apps or tabs.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Local execution does not mean device-only inference; file excerpts, prompts, screenshots, browser content and tool results may be sent to OpenAI.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-overview (links every admin page)

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Conversations follow workspace retention settings with deletion scheduled within 30 days; Compliance Logs Platform keeps 30 days; connected-app data follows the source system.

items.title: Managed deployment and update control
body: Windows ships only as a Store-signed MSIX (no MSI or standalone EXE), deployable via Intune, MECM or winget with offline packages available; macOS deploys from the enterprise DMG, with device management arriving through the com.openai.codex MDM payload rather than a dedicated packaging guide. The built-in updater is disabled with an enforced requirements.toml feature pin, targeted by group, user or platform from the managed-configs console.

items.title: Workspace controls over connectors, apps and memory
body: On Enterprise and Edu workspaces, plugins and their underlying apps are disabled by default and enabled per role, with per-app configuration for real-time access, actions, approvals and domain restrictions — one control set that applies across web, mobile, desktop and Codex. Memory and record mode are workspace-level toggles (record off by default), and the Compliance Logs Platform exports immutable audit, authentication and usage events with 30-day source retention, so longer retention requires continuous export.

links.title: Apps and plugin controls for workspaces

riskNotes.note: Shared connections use the connected account's permissions, which the vendor warns may be broader than the individual user's; Work Local ships file excerpts and screenshots.
The hosted and built-in browsers read arbitrary pages; a review model checks sign-in pages for phishing and Auto approve applies automated risk checks, nothing more.
Agent-owned and shared connected accounts act for whoever triggers the task; action control (read-only or a custom set) is the bound.
Plugins can carry MCP servers, hooks and browser extensions from a GitHub marketplace; Admin > Plugins import and sync is the only provenance record.

App permissions (when ChatGPT asks before using a connection), website approval levels, per-app computer-use approval

variants.name: Codex CLI
Codex IDE extension (openai.chatgpt)
Codex app (ChatGPT desktop, macOS / Windows / Linux)
Codex Remote (phone controls the local app)
Codex GitHub Action (openai/codex-action)
Codex Security (AppSec plugin and CLI)

summary: One agent across the CLI, the IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app, configured through TOML with a documented precedence chain and a genuine enterprise enforcement layer: an admin-authored requirements.toml that constrains approval policies, sandbox profiles, network, MCP servers and feature flags, and that users cannot override.

Inference runs at OpenAI; the local runtime executes commands inside an OS sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap plus seccomp on Linux, a native Windows sandbox) and sends prompts, file excerpts, command output and — when browser or computer use is on — screenshots and page content to OpenAI services. Work Local is explicit that "local execution does not mean offline or device-only model inference". Telemetry is opt-in.

Policy arrives by four channels with a fixed precedence (macOS MDM com.openai.codex, the cloud-managed requirements bundle assigned at chatgpt.com, /etc/codex/requirements.toml or %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml, then managed_config.toml defaults). A cloud bundle that cannot be fetched and has no cache stops the client rather than starting unmanaged. Codex Remote, the GitHub Action and Codex Security are shells of the same runtime; Codex cloud and the SDK are separate entities below.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Codex is in Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu; API-key sign-in pays per token and loses cloud features (GitHub reviews, Slack). Business, Enterprise and Edu add admin controls, Compliance API audit and spend limits.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Model calls go to OpenAI; chatgpt_base_url and model_providers.<id>.base_url can redirect to a proxy, and "Codex respects workspace residency settings when you sign in with ChatGPT".

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, relevant file excerpts, screenshots, browser content and tool results may be sent to OpenAI to complete a task; not every local file operation, screenshot or browser action appears in the Compliance API.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.chatgpt.com/docs (Codex, configuration, enterprise, security sections)

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Workspace audit records are retained up to 30 days for the Compliance API; the BAA does not cover Codex cloud. API-key usage falls under the API data policy (no training by default, 30-day abuse-monitoring logs, ZDR by approval).

items.title: Admin-enforced requirements.toml
body: Requirements arrive by system file (/etc/codex/requirements.toml on Unix, %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml on Windows), as a cloud-managed policy bundle assigned from chatgpt.com and delivered at sign-in, or via macOS MDM under com.openai.codex (base64-encoded TOML; the highest-precedence channel). If the cloud policy fetch fails with no valid cache, the client refuses to start unmanaged rather than failing open.

Enforceable keys cover the surfaces that matter: allowed_approval_policies and allowed_permission_profiles with default_permissions (e.g. pin ":workspace" and allow only read-only and workspace profiles), filesystem deny_read patterns for secrets paths, prefix command rules, managed hooks with allow_managed_hooks_only, experimental network domain allow/deny lists, and feature pins that disable computer use and browser surfaces org-wide.

items.title: Sandbox, approvals and network posture
body: Sandboxing is OS-enforced (Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap plus seccomp on Linux, a native Windows sandbox) with permission profiles from read-only through workspace-write to an explicit danger-full-access escape hatch. The agent runs with network access off by default; enabling it can route through a domain-filtering proxy, and .git, .codex and .agents stay read-only inside writable roots. Codex cloud blocks internet access during the agent phase by default, with per-environment allowlists and method restrictions.

items.title: Workspace gating and compliance export
body: Workspace admins gate Codex Local (desktop app, CLI and IDE extension together) and Codex cloud separately, assign access by role with SCIM-synced groups, and set starting model defaults — enforced requirements still win. Codex usage, including the local clients, exports through the Compliance API and the immutable Compliance Logs Platform alongside workspace audit and authentication logs.

links.title: Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan

riskNotes.note: The vendor's own guidance says prompt injection can make the agent fetch and follow untrusted instructions when network access or web search is on; the 2026 web.run research chained exactly that into out-of-sandbox execution on Windows.
--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (--yolo) removes both boundaries; the admin answer is allowed_approval_policies and allowed_sandbox_modes in requirements.toml, which users cannot loosen.
Plugins bundle MCP servers, skills and hooks from Git marketplaces; without marketplaces.restrict_to_allowed_sources and an [mcp_servers] identity allowlist any developer can add a tool source.
Three 2026 sandbox findings (git show allowlist, Docker socket, ProgramData config trust) were escapes through components the sandbox trusted, not model failures.
File excerpts, screenshots and browser content leave the device on every task; deny_read globs and shell_environment_policy are the only in-product data minimisation.

controls.mechanism: requirements.toml forced_login_method / forced_chatgpt_workspace_id (config) and allowed_login_methods / allowed_chatgpt_workspaces (managed), plus workspace roles and SCIM groups

steps.title: Pin the sign-in method and workspace
body: Set forced_login_method = "chatgpt" and forced_chatgpt_workspace_id = "<uuid>" so the client cannot run on a personal account or an API key.

steps.title: Enforce it from the managed bundle
body: In requirements.toml use allowed_login_methods = ["chatgpt"] and allowed_chatgpt_workspaces as the UUID allowlist; deliver by MDM, cloud policy or the system path.

steps.title: Gate Codex Local by role
body: In Workspace settings > Permissions & roles, set the Codex Local / Work Local permission per role; an explicit Off in any role denies even when another grants.

controls.mechanism: requirements.toml [rules] (forbidden / prompt) and managed [hooks] with allow_managed_hooks_only

steps.title: Write managed command rules
body: Add [rules] entries in requirements.toml with decision "forbidden" or "prompt" for command prefixes; users cannot weaken them.

steps.title: Add a PreToolUse or PermissionRequest hook
body: A managed hook returning permissionDecision "deny" (or exit code 2) blocks the call; set allow_managed_hooks_only = true so user, project and plugin hooks are ignored.

controls.mechanism: Vendor evidence from trust.openai.com consumed by the organisation's TPRM platform
controls.note: OpenAI publishes SOC 2 Type 2 (scope includes API Platform, ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu and Team), ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701/42001, pen-test reports and the subprocessor list on the trust portal; Codex is not named separately, so the assessment inherits the ChatGPT Enterprise scope.

steps.title: Pull vendor evidence
body: Request the SOC 2 report, pen-test summary and subprocessor list from the trust portal and load them into the TPRM record.

controls.mechanism: permissions.filesystem.deny_read globs and shell_environment_policy in requirements.toml
controls.note: These stop the agent reading named paths and environment variables; nothing in the product inspects prompt or upload content. Endpoint DLP is external.

steps.title: Deny reads of secret paths
body: Set [permissions.filesystem] deny_read globs (SSH keys, cloud credentials, .env); full-access profiles are rejected while deny-read rules exist.

steps.title: Strip secrets from the shell environment
body: Set shell_environment_policy.inherit = "core" and exclude patterns so tokens in the developer's environment never reach subprocesses.

controls.mechanism: allowed_permission_profiles, default_permissions, allowed_sandbox_modes, [mcp_servers] enabled_tools / disabled_tools and [features] pins in requirements.toml

steps.title: Fix the permission profile set
body: Set allowed_permission_profiles (the complete allowlist; omitted profiles are denied) and default_permissions = ":workspace"; add allowed_sandbox_modes.

steps.title: Scope MCP tools per server
body: In each [mcp_servers.<name>] set enabled_tools or disabled_tools and a default_tools_approval_mode.

steps.title: Pin high-agency features off
body: Set [features] computer_use = false, browser_use = false and browser_use_full_cdp_access = false where the fleet does not need them.

controls.mechanism: OS sandbox (Seatbelt / bubblewrap+seccomp / Windows sandbox) selected by sandbox_mode and pinned by allowed_sandbox_modes
controls.note: Three 2026 escapes (git show allowlist, Docker socket, ProgramData config trust) sit in advisories; the Docker-socket one is by design unless a socket is explicitly allowed.

steps.title: Understand the boundary
body: workspace-write keeps writes inside the workspace and network off; .git, .agents and .codex under writable roots stay read-only.

steps.title: Remove the escape hatch
body: Pin allowed_sandbox_modes to ["read-only", "workspace-write"] so danger-full-access and --yolo are unavailable.

controls.mechanism: cli_auth_credentials_store, scoped access tokens and service accounts
controls.note: Locally the agent acts as the signed-in developer with that developer's file and git rights; there is no on-behalf-of exchange. Automation can run as a service account so runs attribute to a non-human identity.

steps.title: Keep credentials out of auth.json
body: Set cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring" (or "ephemeral" for CI) in requirements.toml.

steps.title: Run automation as a service account
body: Create a service account, assign it plugins and a role, and issue CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN from its Access tokens section (CLI 0.142.0+).

controls.mechanism: history.persistence and the Computer History role permission
controls.note: Codex keeps session transcripts under CODEX_HOME and, on the desktop app, a searchable Computer History; there is no admin validation or quarantine of that store.

steps.title: Disable local transcript persistence
body: Set [history] persistence = "none" (and max_bytes) in the managed config.

steps.title: Gate Computer History by role
body: Workspace settings > Permissions & roles carries the Computer History permission.

controls.mechanism: Guardian automatic review (allowed_approvals_reviewers, guardian_policy_config) and the browser sign-in review model
controls.note: The vendor ships a reviewing model for out-of-sandbox requests and for browser sign-in pages, and warns that refusal is probabilistic; no admin-tunable classifier on inputs.

steps.title: Decide whether automatic review may replace the human
body: allowed_approvals_reviewers controls whether ["auto_review"] is permitted; guardian_policy_config overrides the review policy text.

steps.title: Keep web access off where it is not needed
body: Network access defaults off in workspace-write; the docs say prompt injection can make the agent fetch and follow untrusted instructions once it is on.

controls.mechanism: OS keyring credential store, workspace access-token expiration limit, workload identity federation

steps.title: Cap token lifetime
body: Owners set "Access token expiration limit" in Permissions & roles; tokens are created at chatgpt.com/admin/access-tokens with a required expiry.

steps.title: Replace stored tokens with federation
body: Exchange an OIDC or SPIFFE token via OPENAI_FEDERATION_RULE_ID / OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE; the resulting token never lasts longer than one hour.

controls.mechanism: requirements.toml [mcp_servers] identity allowlist and [marketplaces] restrict_to_allowed_sources

steps.title: Allowlist MCP servers by identity
body: A server is enabled only when both its name and identity match an approved [mcp_servers] entry; an empty table disables all MCP servers.

steps.title: Restrict plugin sources
body: Set [marketplaces] with restrict_to_allowed_sources = true and pin features.plugins; unmatched marketplace operations are rejected.

controls.mechanism: allowed_approval_policies in requirements.toml and the permission modes

steps.title: Require approval outside the sandbox
body: Set allowed_approval_policies = ["on-request"] (or add "untrusted"); "never" is then unavailable.

steps.title: Keep Full access out of the mode picker
body: Ask for approval, Approve for me (auto-review) and Full access are the user modes; admins decide which profiles the workspace allows.

controls.mechanism: Admin > Plugins marketplace import and the [mcp_servers] approved identities
controls.note: Approved plugins and MCP servers are recorded centrally; nothing inventories the local agents or MCP servers a developer runs outside that list.

steps.title: Manage the plugin catalogue
body: Admin > Plugins imports a GitHub marketplace, syncs daily and sets Available or Installed per role.

controls.mechanism: [otel] OTLP export from the client and the workspace Compliance API
controls.note: The Compliance API keeps records 30 days; Work Local warns that not every local file operation, screenshot or browser action appears there. OTel is opt-in per client.

steps.title: Export client events
body: Set [otel] exporter = "otlp-http" or "otlp-grpc" with your endpoint; log_user_prompt defaults to false (redacted).

steps.title: Pull workspace records
body: Use the Compliance API with COMPLIANCE_API_KEY; the Admin API reference is the source of truth for event coverage and retention.

controls.mechanism: None in product; forced workspace login turns personal-account use into a detectable violation
controls.note: Discover unmanaged installs (npm @openai/codex, the openai.chatgpt extension, the MSIX) with EDR or software inventory; allowed_chatgpt_workspaces then blocks personal accounts.

controls.mechanism: Role permission off, token revocation, service-account disable, federation rule disable

steps.title: Turn the surface off
body: Set "Allow members to use Codex locally" (or the combined Codex and Work Locally toggle) to Off for the affected roles.

steps.title: Revoke automation credentials
body: Owners and admins revoke any workspace access token; disabling a service account revokes all of its tokens.

controls.mechanism: EDR rules around the runtime; no vendor hook for endpoint security products
controls.note: Watch for batch or executable files created in project roots (web.run node.bat chain), Docker-socket use from the agent, and non-admin writes under %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex; pre-create and ACL that directory (CVE-2026-35603).

controls.mechanism: AGENTS.md hierarchy with project_doc_max_bytes and project trust
controls.note: Instructions load from ~/.codex/AGENTS.md then repo-root-to-cwd AGENTS.md files; project config loads only for trusted projects. There is no admin-owned instruction file.

steps.title: Own the instruction files
body: Keep AGENTS.md under code review; AGENTS.override.md wins at each level and project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default) truncates the merged set.

controls.mechanism: Not offered
controls.note: No signed manifest of runtime, plugins or MCP servers; the closest is codex-version pinning in the GitHub Action and marketplace sync from a Git source.

controls.mechanism: [experimental_network] managed_allowed_domains_only and sandbox_workspace_write.network_access
controls.note: Domain rules apply to command proxying inside the sandbox, not to browser tools, web search or MCP servers; those need a network-layer control.

steps.title: Allowlist domains for sandboxed commands
body: In requirements.toml set [experimental_network] allowed and denied domains with managed_allowed_domains_only = true.

steps.title: Keep network off by default
body: sandbox_workspace_write.network_access = false is the default; features.network_proxy adds allow/deny domain maps when it is on.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable
controls.note: No model artifacts are loaded locally; model_provider can point at a local server (ollama, lmstudio), which brings the organisation's own scanning obligation.

summary: Codex cloud runs coding tasks in OpenAI-hosted containers built from the universal image plus a per-environment setup script, checked out from a GitHub or GitLab repository and started from the web, the IDE extension, Slack, Linear, a pull request comment or a schedule. The same hosted harness is what ChatGPT Work calls Work Cloud, which the vendor describes as VM-backed sandboxes on OpenAI infrastructure.

Inference and execution are both at OpenAI: the repository, environment variables and the prompt leave the organisation, and the agent's output returns as a diff or pull request for a human to merge. Internet access during the agent phase is off by default and is set per environment (Off, On, On with controls with a domain allowlist and GET/HEAD/ OPTIONS-only methods); secrets are encrypted, exposed only to setup scripts and removed before the agent phase.

Admin gating is by workspace role (Work Cloud / Codex cloud toggles, GitHub connector), by environment (internet, repositories, secrets) and by connector setting (the Slack posting toggle, Codex for Linear). Compliance API records are retained 30 days; the BAA does not cover Codex cloud.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Cloud features require Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu; not available on Free, Go or API-key sign-in.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Tasks run in OpenAI-hosted containers behind an HTTP/HTTPS proxy; caches are shared across users with access to the environment on Business and Enterprise.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: The repository checkout, environment variables, uploaded context, Slack thread history or Linear issue content are sent to create the cloud chat.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Conversations follow workspace retention with deletion scheduled within 30 days; execution snapshots and Library files follow separate lifecycles; Compliance Logs Platform keeps records 30 days.

riskNotes.note: The internet-access page shows hidden instructions in fetched web content driving secret exfiltration; the default Off and GET-only controls are the mitigation.
Cached containers are shared across every user with access to the environment for up to 12 hours, so anything a setup script writes is visible to the next user's task.
Output is a diff or PR, but automatic reviews and Slack posting act without a prompt; scope the GitHub app and the "post answers" toggle.
Environments and setup scripts are editable by anyone with access; they run with internet on.

controls.mechanism: Workspace roles (Work Cloud / Codex cloud permission) and SCIM groups

steps.title: Gate cloud execution by role
body: Workspace settings > Permissions & roles carries Work Cloud and Work Local as distinct toggles; enable Work Cloud selectively.

steps.title: Provision membership from the IdP
body: SCIM provisions membership and group assignment; groups need explicit role grants and an Off in any role denies.

controls.mechanism: Service accounts (SCIM userType ServiceAccount) and the GitLab service-account token
controls.note: Runs attribute to a service account; the GitHub App identity itself is vendor-owned.

steps.title: Create a non-human workspace identity
body: Owners and admins create service accounts with their own plugins, role and tokens; disabling the account revokes every token.

steps.title: Scope the GitLab connector
body: Use an existing service account with Developer access to selected groups or projects; admins can revoke and regenerate its token in Codex Cloud settings.

controls.mechanism: Environment secrets (encrypted, setup-script only) versus environment variables

steps.title: Put credentials in Secrets, not variables
body: Secrets get an additional layer of encryption, are only available to setup scripts and are removed before the agent phase; environment variables persist.

tools.name: Codex SDK

variants.name: @openai/codex-sdk (TypeScript)
openai-codex (Python)

summary: The SDK embeds the Codex agent in customer-hosted automation: it drives a local Codex runtime (the Python package pins its own) over JSON-RPC with a thread/turn API, sandbox presets (read_only, workspace_write, full_access) settable per thread or per turn, and model selection. Inference is at OpenAI; execution is wherever the host runs.

Because it is the same app-server, the host's config.toml and any requirements.toml apply — the SDK page says an omitted sandbox falls back to the app-server's configured default. Unattended runs authenticate with CODEX_API_KEY, a service-account CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN or workload identity federation, which is the credential story that distinguishes this entity from the interactive shells.

Runs act as whichever token the host holds; use a service account so actions attribute to the automation, not an engineer.

tools.name: Secure MCP Tunnel (tunnel-client)

variants.name: tunnel-client (binary and ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client container)

summary: Secure MCP Tunnel lets a private or localhost MCP server serve ChatGPT developer-mode apps, the Responses API and Codex without inbound exposure: a customer-run tunnel-client polls api.openai.com (or mtls.api.openai.com) over outbound HTTPS, forwards each request to the local stdio or HTTP MCP server, and returns the response through the same tunnel.

The tunnel itself carries no inference; it is the connectivity leg between OpenAI's hosted chat and the organisation's tool server, which is why it sits on the enterprise-chat architecture. Tunnels are created, rotated and revoked in Platform tunnel settings, are scoped to one or more Platform organisations or ChatGPT workspaces, authenticate with a runtime API key (CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY) and optionally mTLS in both directions, and support outbound proxies and custom CA bundles.

Audit is split: tunnel.created / updated / deleted appear in Platform audit logs, but control-plane tunnel traffic is not emitted as Compliance Platform app events; app-level invocation and auth-lifecycle logging still applies when ChatGPT reaches the app through the tunnel.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Platform organisation permissions (Tunnels Read / Read + Manage / Read + Use); ChatGPT developer-mode access is granted separately by workspace admins.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: No inference; requests are polled from api.openai.com:443 or mtls.api.openai.com:443 and forwarded to the private MCP server.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: MCP requests and responses transit OpenAI's control plane; the MCP server address stays private to the tunnel-client environment.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Tunnel traffic is not emitted as Compliance Platform app events; app-level logs apply. API data is not used for training by default.

riskNotes.note: A tunnel can be associated with several organisations or workspaces; every association is a tenant that can reach the private server.
The tunnel presents one runtime key; per-user authorization has to happen in the MCP server or the app's auth flow.
Rotation and revocation are manual in Platform tunnel settings; a forgotten tunnel keeps polling.

tools.name: OpenClaw
summary: A self-hosted personal agent whose gateway is the control plane — channels, tool policy and auth under an explicit single-trusted-operator model. Official hardening is real and specific: loopback-plus-token gateway auth, DM pairing, high-risk tools disabled or sandboxed, and a container sandbox whose defaults are no network, a read-only root and all capabilities dropped.

items.title: Gateway lockdown and the version floor
body: The gateway defaults to loopback binding; the docs say plainly never to expose it unauthenticated on 0.0.0.0, and token auth is the recommended mode. DM hardening is dmPolicy pairing (time-limited codes for unknown senders), contact allowlists and requireMention in groups; `openclaw security audit` checks a deployment and can apply safe fixes. Enforce a version floor of 2026.1.29: earlier Control UI builds auto-connected to an attacker-supplied gatewayUrl and sent the operator token (CVE-2026-25253, CVSS 8.8), and internet scans found thousands of exposed instances.

items.title: Sandbox defaults and proxy-injected credentials
body: With the Docker sandbox backend enabled, tool execution runs in a container whose defaults are network none, readOnlyRoot true, all capabilities dropped and a non-root user, with the workspace mounted read-only or read-write by policy; per-agent sandbox and tool-policy overrides layer on top, and the docs warn never to mount the Docker socket into a sandbox. Docker's own Sandboxes product wraps the same agent with a configurable egress proxy that denies arbitrary hosts and injects provider API keys at the proxy, so the agent process never holds them.
